sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: phase_tracker
toolsAdded.description: Track workflow phase progress (brainstorm → plan → implement → verify → ship); ad-hoc calls do not arm gates. Not for ad-hoc use.

phase.description: Phase name (required for start, complete, skip)

reason.description: Reason (required for skip and grant_fix_rounds; for grant, the human's approval quoted)

rounds.description: Extra fix rounds the human explicitly approved (grant_fix_rounds only)

force.description: Reset and re-start a phase that is already complete or skipped (rare; default false)

substep.description: Substep label for action=substep on an in_progress phase; null or omitted clears it

toolsAdded.name: plan_tracker
toolsAdded.description: Track progress while EXECUTING an implementation plan (the implement phase), a verify-phase conformance fix wave, or another bounded gate checklist (e.g. pre-merge PR verification). Statuses: pending (not yet touched), in_progress (started; several at once is fine), complete, failed (terminal-negative: ran and did not pass; never counted done), skipped (terminal: not applicable in this run; counted done). Rule: pending tasks must trail every started or finished task - an update that would leave a pending task ahead of a non-pending one is rejected with the fix. update never sets pending; init and add do. Actions: init (set task list; elements are task-name strings or { name, status } to recreate a list with known statuses), add (append tasks as pending; existing statuses preserved), update (change task status), status (show current state), clear (remove plan), refresh (derive tasks from an artifact path while retaining other tasks). Do NOT use for brainstorming, research, or planning checklists: those phases are open-ended and a bounded task list misrepresents them as a fixed N-step process.

path.description: Artifact path for refresh; relative paths resolve against the session cwd

status.description: Status to recreate the task with (init only)

tasks.description: Tasks for init and add. A string is a pending task. init also accepts { name, status } to recreate a list with known statuses (fresh session, amendment re-init); the whole list must satisfy the pending-suffix rule.

status.description: New status (for update). failed is terminal-negative (ran and did not pass); skipped is terminal, not applicable in this run, counted as done. pending is set only by init/add; to redo a task, reopen it as in_progress, or re-init with {name, status}[] to recreate a whole list.

toolsAdded.name: plan_check
toolsAdded.description: Deterministically verify an implementation plan against its spec (mechanical checks); a pass stamps the plan for implement-start.

planPath.description: Path to the implementation plan (absolute, or relative to cwd)

toolsAdded.name: gauntlet_setting
toolsAdded.description: Resolve merged piGauntlet.* settings (repo over preset); for skill use only.

key.description: Which gauntlet setting to resolve (merged repo-over-preset).

name: gauntlet-resume
description: Use when a human wants to continue an interrupted gauntlet flow in a fresh session - from a gauntlet-handoff brief (file, pasted, or picked from the default handoff directory), from a bare worktree that already holds a spec, or from a spec tracked on main (creates or reuses its worktree via `/skill:using-git-worktrees`). Human-only; the sole resume entry point. Restores phase/plan tracker state through the legal arming sequence, never infers approval.
disable-model-invocation: true
argument-hint: "[<brief-file> | <spec>.md | <worktree-name-or-path>]"
---

> **Related skills:** Continues into `/skill:writing-plans`, `/skill:subagent-driven-development`, `/skill:loop-implementation`, or `/skill:verification-before-completion` depending on the restored stage.

# Gauntlet Resume

## Overview

Re-enter an interrupted gauntlet flow in a fresh session. Three inputs: a handoff brief
produced by `/skill:gauntlet-handoff` (grammar in `reference/brief-contract.md`), a bare
worktree whose spec/plan artifacts are reconstructed into tracker state
(`reference/reconstruction.md`), a spec seed (`reference/seed.md`). Every check runs
before any tracker mutation; every stop names the offending path, field, or line.
`Read` each reference in full at the step that names it, never from memory; a missing
or unreadable reference stops the route, naming its path.

**Announce at start (after the marker on marked messages):** "I'm using the gauntlet-resume skill to continue an interrupted flow."

## Boundaries

- Reads: anything.
- Writes: `phase_tracker` / `plan_tracker` state after every check passes and every
  human question is answered; the plan file, only through the plan repair that
  `reference/restore-plan.md` enters on a `plan_check` FAIL; the ledger through `reference/restore-loop.md` "Pending recovery" and the loop driver's admission/repair contract; on the seed route, what `/skill:using-git-worktrees` writes. Never a spec copy, rename, or marker commit.
- Never: `git worktree add` directly; worktree creation by resume itself only on
  the seed route, only through `/skill:using-git-worktrees`; infer approval from
  artifact presence; restore
  gate history, closure-review evidence, or fix rounds; start a later phase directly
  (that does not arm the flow).

## Arguments

`/skill:gauntlet-resume [<token>] [<worktree>]` - zero to two positional tokens, plus
optional pasted text after the command line. Count tokens first; then first match wins.
Spec dirs resolve per `reference/reconstruction.md` "Candidates" (`flowGuards.specDirs`
precedence).

Read and apply [menu-layout](../brainstorming/reference/menu-layout.md) before presenting these options and before acting on a numeric reply.

For the discovery menu, start the message with the marker specified below. Start the message with `gauntlet: gate=gauntlet-resume/discovery`.
For no briefs and every stop route in the table, end without mutation. Start the message with `gauntlet: stuck` followed by the existing reason on that line.

| Input | Route |
|---|---|
| no tokens, no pasted text | discovery: `<tmpdir>` via `node -p "require('os').tmpdir()"`; candidates are the regular files directly under `<tmpdir>/pi-handoff/` ending `.md` (non-recursive) whose line 1 starts `# Handoff:`; sorted by mtime, newest first; displayed one per line as `<n>. <title line> - <worktree: field value> - <mtime ISO-8601>` with `worktree: unavailable` when the field is absent; the human picks `<n>` (a single candidate is still confirmed); none -> STOP "no handoff briefs found under <tmpdir>/pi-handoff" |
| pasted text, line 1 starts `# Handoff:` | brief |
| two tokens, first an existing file with line 1 `# Handoff:` | brief with worktree override: required when the brief's worktree field is `no`/`unavailable`/not a git repo; must equal the brief's worktree after `realpath` otherwise |
| two tokens, first a spec seed | stop: `a spec seed takes no worktree: <second token>` |
| one token, existing regular file, line 1 starts `# Handoff:` | brief |
| one token, existing regular file ending `.md`, `realpath` under `<primary>/<specDir>` | spec seed - `reference/seed.md` |
| one token, existing regular file, anything else | stop: `not a handoff brief and not under <specDirs>: <path>` |
| one token, existing directory that is a git worktree root (`git -C <dir> rev-parse --show-toplevel` equals its `realpath`) other than `<primary>` | worktree |
| one token, missing path (ends `.md` or contains a separator) | stop: `not found: <path>` |
| one token, bare name | worktree at `<primary>/.worktrees/<name>`; missing or not a git worktree -> entry check 2 stop |
| anything else | stop: "this is a new idea - run /skill:brainstorming" |

A relative token resolves against the session cwd; a bare `name.md` absent there is
tried at `<primary>/<specDir>/name.md` per resolved spec dir in order, first hit wins.
`<primary>` is the checkout owning `.worktrees/`:
`dirname "$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)"` run in the session
cwd - absolute from any primary subdirectory and from inside a linked worktree
(`--show-toplevel` would return the linked worktree there). A pasted brief that needs
an override uses the file form. A brief then runs entry checks 1-6, so a stale or
foreign-repo brief stops there.

## Entry checks

For an entry-check stop, retain the offending path, field, or line. Start the message with `gauntlet: stuck` followed by the reason on that line.

In order. All before any tracker mutation; entry check 1 is read-only. A spec
seed runs check 1 here, then `reference/seed.md`, which runs check 3 itself;
checks 2, 4, 5 do not apply; check 6 runs on the seed's pinned spec path.

For a brief, `Read` `reference/brief-contract.md` in full before check 2.

**Membership test.** A brief that carries a `legs:` block is multi-repo: `Read` `reference/coordinated.md` in full before check 3 and apply it at
checks 3, 3b and 4, before any tracker write. Without that block, read nothing from
that file.

1. **Idle session.** `phase_tracker({ action: "status" })`. Any phase not pending ->
   stop: "session already carries flow state - reset is your call".
2. **Target worktree.** Resolve from the brief's `worktree:` field, the override, or the
   bare argument. Stops: path missing or `git -C <path> rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`
   fails; override and brief worktree differ after `realpath`; brief has no
   `## Repo state` heading (prefix match); brief worktree is `no`, `unavailable`, or
   `not a git repo` and no override was given - except a `worktree: no` brief **without**
   process state, which is the brainstorming route in Dispatch, not a stop. Other
   `unavailable` fields inside `## Repo state` are legal.
3. **Same-repository binding.** Settings and flow guards come from the repository in
   the extension's session cwd. Compare
   `realpath "$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)"` in the session
   cwd with
   `realpath "$(git -C <worktree> rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)"`.
   If they differ, stop, name both paths, and say the resolved worktree belongs to a
   different repository; restart pi in that repository's primary checkout and re-run.
   Same-repository worktrees proceed by path: use `git -C <worktree>` for
   worktree Git commands and absolute artifact paths for `Read` and `plan_check`.
4. **Drift notice.** Compare the brief's `HEAD` and `dirty` fields in `## Repo state`
   with the live worktree (`git -C <worktree> rev-parse HEAD`, `git -C <worktree>
   status --porcelain`). Announce differences. Informational, never a stop.
5. **Skills loaded.** For each name in `## Skills loaded` (none for
   `## Skills loaded: none`): match against the frontmatter `name` of every
   `skills/*/SKILL.md` in this package; `Read` each match's complete file into the
   transcript; list non-matches as skipped. Loaded bodies are context only - no skill's
   entry actions run until Dispatch names one.
6. **Grant field.** Run deferred-header admission whenever a route resolves an existing spec, including brainstorm-stage process-state restore and reconstruction's unapproved-draft handoff, before any tracker mutation or brainstorming invocation. Carry the resolved `<spec path>` without re-resolving it: use the restore reference's path, `reference/reconstruction.md`, or the seed's pinned `<full-path>/<rel>` (`reference/seed.md`).
   Read the spec's header block (between the H1 and the first `##`). An exact `**Engine:** deferred` stops with `spec approved for handoff only - run brainstorming #N`; make no phase_tracker or plan_tracker mutation. After deferred-header admission, apply the grant predicate only for an approved spec in
   [Standing grants](../brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md#standing-grants): no
   `**Amend-grant:**` line -> no grant;
   exactly one line whose trimmed value is `none` -> no grant;
   exactly one line whose trimmed value is any other non-empty single-line text ->
   grant active, the sentence is that value;
   two or more lines, one line with an empty value, or a value continued onto the next physical line ->
   malformed, stop, print the offending line(s), no tracker call. Skip only grant decoding for routes that resolve no
   approved spec (hotfix, `worktree: no`, a brief whose active phase is brainstorm,
   reconstruction's unapproved-draft brainstorming handoff); print no grant line.
   Resume reports the line; it never writes it.

## Dispatch

For the `worktree: no` brainstorming offer, keep the explicit-selection wait. Start the message with exactly `gauntlet: question` on its own line, with no suffix.

| Input | Route |
|---|---|
| brief with `## Process state` and a `Ledger:` field | `reference/reconstruction.md`, then `reference/restore-loop.md`: "Ledger admission", "Spec with ledger" |
| brief with `## Process state` and no `Ledger:` field, at any stage | `reference/reconstruction.md`, then `reference/restore-plan.md`: "Process-state restore" |
| brief without process state, `## Skills loaded` names `chase-bug` | hotfix route below, before any artifact reconstruction, no tracker calls |
| brief without process state, `worktree: no` | offer `/skill:brainstorming` with `## Intent` as the idea and wait for explicit selection; then invoke [`/skill:brainstorming`](../brainstorming/SKILL.md) in the current directory; resume creates no worktree - brainstorming's own Worktree First applies (a plain handoff is a new flow) |
| brief without process state, worktree present | `reference/reconstruction.md` |
| bare worktree | `reference/reconstruction.md` |
| spec seed | `reference/seed.md` |

**Engine test.** The two process-state rows above select by the `Ledger:` field alone,
whatever the spec's `**Engine:**`. On the other routes, after "Candidates" has classified
the artifacts: one spec with a ledger (a plan-dir file whose line 1 is
`# Ledger - loop engine`; takes precedence over a task plan) -> `reference/restore-loop.md`;
one spec with a task plan only, or seed step 8 finding a plan beside the pinned spec ->
`reference/restore-plan.md` "Spec with plan"; no spec, more than one spec, or one spec
without a plan -> no restore reference, the route stays in `reference/reconstruction.md`.

**Hotfix route.** `skills/chase-bug/hotfix.md` consumes only a hotfix record at
`$TMPDIR/hotfix-<slug>.md`. If `## Decisions` or `## Intent` names an existing record
path, hand it to hotfix.md and skip its worktree-create step when the brief's worktree
exists (reuse it). Otherwise invoke `/skill:chase-bug` triage with `## Intent` to
re-derive the record.

## Restore rules

Facts that fix the arming order:

- Arming happens only on `start brainstorm`; `reset` disarms; `skip` and `complete`
  preserve it.
- `plan_check` stamps only inside an armed flow; unarmed it returns
  `PASS (no flow to stamp)`.
- `start implement` is rejected without a current `plan_check` stamp.
- `skip` has no state precondition and takes a `reason`; one phase is active at a time.
- `complete verify` is blocked without a fresh `conformance-reviewer` dispatch when
  closure review is enforced.
- `plan_tracker init` on an in-progress implement with every task `complete`/`skipped`
  auto-completes implement.

"Exact" restoration binds: the active phase identity and substep, and the plan task list
(names, order, statuses) verbatim. Prior phases show `⊘ (resume: ...)` regardless of the
brief's glyph - skip-arming is the mechanism and completing priors would fabricate gated
history. `No plan active.` -> no `init` call.

Before `init`, validate feasibility against the tracker's own rules:

- pending-suffix order - every `○` task must trail every non-pending task;
- the implement auto-complete edge - an implement brief whose tasks are all
  complete/skipped is infeasible as stated; propose verify as the target and ask.

Every restore ends with the closing line:

```
Gate history not restored; re-validating `<task>` before any stage advance
```

`<task>` is `ledger rows` for a ledger; for a task plan it is the brief's `Active task`,
else the first in-progress task, else `none` (whole-deliverable re-validation).

## Post-restore continuation

A successful restore is an automatic handoff, not a terminal report; let the resumed skill own the next ask and its marker. Keep the brief fields unchanged and infer no approval. After plan repair of a plan that was dirty or untracked before repair, state explicitly that the repair stays in the working copy and lands with the next task commit; run no `git add` or repair commit.

After a successful restore, print the closing line, then on its own line exactly one of `Standing grant active: <sentence>` or `No standing grant.` from check 6 (nothing when grant decoding was skipped), then continue in the stage's
owning skill **without** its reset-bearing entry:

| Active after restore | Continue in | Entry point |
|---|---|---|
| brainstorm | [brainstorming checklist](../brainstorming/SKILL.md#checklist) | on-disk state decides the step: draft marker on line 1 of the spec file -> step 4; spec title -> step 8. Never `/skill:brainstorming` entry (it resets both trackers) |
| approved spec with `**Engine:** loop`, no ledger | loop-implementation | Entry steps 1-5, carried and labeled as `reference/reconstruction.md` "Spec without plan" states; a restored plan-stage brief makes no second arming call |
| plan with task engine | writing-plans body | skip its `start plan` call (already in_progress) |
| implement with a ledger | loop-implementation | `reference/restore-loop.md` "Spec with ledger" step 9: `Before each dispatch`; reuse the existing ledger |
| implement with task plan | subagent-driven-development | re-validate `<task>` first (re-run its `Tests:`), then the task loop from the first non-complete task |
| verify with `Ledger:` (including ship-stage ledger briefs restored at verify) | /skill:loop-implementation | `reference/restore-loop.md` "Spec with ledger" step 9: `After the loop` step 1; never start implement |
| verify without `Ledger:` | verification-before-completion | full conformance gate; nothing carried over |

## Red flags — STOP

- Any `phase_tracker` or `plan_tracker` mutation before the route's entry checks pass and
  every human question is answered.
- `start <phase>` for anything other than brainstorm as the first arming call.
- `complete` on a prior phase during restore (priors are `skip`ped with a `resume:` reason).
- Running `git worktree add` directly, or `cd`-ing to "fix" a cwd mismatch.
- Accepting a free-form prompt as a brief.

## Project overrides
If a gauntlet overrides file exists - checked in order:
`.pi/gauntlet-overrides.md`, `<repo root>/gauntlet-overrides.md`,
`<repo root>/doc/gauntlet-overrides.md`; first found wins - read it once per session - a skill that already has the file's content in context from an earlier skill's read skips the read; a restored session has nothing in context and reads it. Read
and apply `## conventions` whenever present, without a relevance
judgment.
Give this skill's named section precedence over conflicting
`## conventions` rules. Use other relevant sections - by name match,
by topic (routing,
verification, worktrees, etc.), or by workflow convention - to override or
extend the instructions above. Project-local `AGENTS.md` is already in
context - check it for project-specific routing tables, service paths, and
verification commands.

The recognized headings, their readers, and the rules an override cannot change are listed in the [configuration front door](../../README.md#project-specific-overrides); an override extends or replaces the step it names and never lifts this skill's HARD CONSTRAINT or MUST text.

judgment.

by topic (routing,

extend the instructions above. Project-local `AGENTS.md` is already in
context - check it for project-specific routing tables, service paths, and
verification commands.

   [Standing grants](../brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md#standing-grants): no
   `**Amend-grant:**` line -> no grant;
   exactly one line whose trimmed value is `none` -> no grant;
   exactly one line whose trimmed value is any other non-empty single-line text ->
   grant active, the sentence is that value;
   two or more lines, one line with an empty value, or a value continued onto the next physical line ->
   malformed, stop, print the offending line(s), no tracker call. Skip only grant decoding for routes that resolve no
   approved spec (hotfix, `worktree: no`, a brief whose active phase is brainstorm,
   reconstruction's unapproved-draft brainstorming handoff); print no grant line.
   Resume reports the line; it never writes it.

## Dispatch

For the `worktree: no` brainstorming offer, keep the explicit-selection wait. Start the message with exactly `gauntlet: question` on its own line, with no suffix.

| Input | Route |
|---|---|
| brief with `## Process state` and a `Ledger:` field | `reference/reconstruction.md`, then `reference/restore-loop.md`: "Ledger admission", "Spec with ledger" |
| brief with `## Process state` and no `Ledger:` field, at any stage | `reference/reconstruction.md`, then `reference/restore-plan.md`: "Process-state restore" |
| brief without process state, `## Skills loaded` names `chase-bug` | hotfix route below, before any artifact reconstruction, no tracker calls |
| brief without process state, `worktree: no` | offer `/skill:brainstorming` with `## Intent` as the idea and wait for explicit selection; then invoke [`/skill:brainstorming`](../brainstorming/SKILL.md) in the current directory; resume creates no worktree - brainstorming's own Worktree First applies (a plain handoff is a new flow) |
| brief without process state, worktree present | `reference/reconstruction.md` |
| bare worktree | `reference/reconstruction.md` |
| spec seed | `reference/seed.md` |

**Engine test.** The two process-state rows above select by the `Ledger:` field alone,
whatever the spec's `**Engine:**`. On the other routes, after "Candidates" has classified
the artifacts: one spec with a ledger (a plan-dir file whose line 1 is
`# Ledger - loop engine`; takes precedence over a task plan) -> `reference/restore-loop.md`;
one spec with a task plan only, or seed step 8 finding a plan beside the pinned spec ->
`reference/restore-plan.md` "Spec with plan"; no spec, more than one spec, or one spec
without a plan -> no restore reference, the route stays in `reference/reconstruction.md`.

**Hotfix route.** `skills/chase-bug/hotfix.md` consumes only a hotfix record at
`$TMPDIR/hotfix-<slug>.md`. If `## Decisions` or `## Intent` names an existing record
path, hand it to hotfix.md and skip its worktree-create step when the brief's worktree
exists (reuse it). Otherwise invoke `/skill:chase-bug` triage with `## Intent` to
re-derive the record.

## Restore rules

Facts that fix the arming order:

- Arming happens only on `start brainstorm`; `reset` disarms; `skip` and `complete`
  preserve it.
- `plan_check` stamps only inside an armed flow; unarmed it returns
  `PASS (no flow to stamp)`.
- `start implement` is rejected without a current `plan_check` stamp.
- `skip` has no state precondition and takes a `reason`; one phase is active at a time.
- `complete verify` is blocked without a fresh `conformance-reviewer` dispatch when
  closure review is enforced.
- `plan_tracker init` on an in-progress implement with every task `complete`/`skipped`
  auto-completes implement.

"Exact" restoration binds: the active phase identity and substep, and the plan task list
(names, order, statuses) verbatim. Prior phases show `⊘ (resume: ...)` regardless of the
brief's glyph - skip-arming is the mechanism and completing priors would fabricate gated
history. `No plan active.` -> no `init` call.

Before `init`, validate feasibility against the tracker's own rules:

- pending-suffix order - every `○` task must trail every non-pending task;
- the implement auto-complete edge - an implement brief whose tasks are all
  complete/skipped is infeasible as stated; propose verify as the target and ask.

Every restore ends with the closing line:

```
Gate history not restored; re-validating `<task>` before any stage advance
```

`<task>` is `ledger rows` for a ledger; for a task plan it is the brief's `Active task`,
else the first in-progress task, else `none` (whole-deliverable re-validation).

## Post-restore continuation

A successful restore is an automatic handoff, not a terminal report; let the resumed skill own the next ask and its marker. Keep the brief fields unchanged and infer no approval. After plan repair of a plan that was dirty or untracked before repair, state explicitly that the repair stays in the working copy and lands with the next task commit; run no `git add` or repair commit.

After a successful restore, print the closing line, then on its own line exactly one of `Standing grant active: <sentence>` or `No standing grant.` from check 6 (nothing when grant decoding was skipped), then continue in the stage's
owning skill **without** its reset-bearing entry:

| Active after restore | Continue in | Entry point |
|---|---|---|
| brainstorm | [brainstorming checklist](../brainstorming/SKILL.md#checklist) | on-disk state decides the step: draft marker on line 1 of the spec file -> step 4; spec title -> step 8. Never `/skill:brainstorming` entry (it resets both trackers) |
| approved spec with `**Engine:** loop`, no ledger | loop-implementation | Entry steps 1-5, carried and labeled as `reference/reconstruction.md` "Spec without plan" states; a restored plan-stage brief makes no second arming call |
| plan with task engine | writing-plans body | skip its `start plan` call (already in_progress) |
| implement with a ledger | loop-implementation | `reference/restore-loop.md` "Spec with ledger" step 9: `Before each dispatch`; reuse the existing ledger |
| implement with task plan | subagent-driven-development | re-validate `<task>` first (re-run its `Tests:`), then the task loop from the first non-complete task |
| verify with `Ledger:` (including ship-stage ledger briefs restored at verify) | /skill:loop-implementation | `reference/restore-loop.md` "Spec with ledger" step 9: `After the loop` step 1; never start implement |
| verify without `Ledger:` | verification-before-completion | full conformance gate; nothing carried over |

## Red flags — STOP

- Any `phase_tracker` or `plan_tracker` mutation before the route's entry checks pass and
  every human question is answered.
- `start <phase>` for anything other than brainstorm as the first arming call.
- `complete` on a prior phase during restore (priors are `skip`ped with a `resume:` reason).
- Running `git worktree add` directly, or `cd`-ing to "fix" a cwd mismatch.
- Accepting a free-form prompt as a brief.

## Project overrides
If a gauntlet overrides file exists - checked in order:
`.pi/gauntlet-overrides.md`, `<repo root>/gauntlet-overrides.md`,
`<repo root>/doc/gauntlet-overrides.md`; first found wins - read it once per session - a skill that already has the file's content in context from an earlier skill's read skips the read; a restored session has nothing in context and reads it. Read
and apply `## conventions` whenever present, without a relevance
judgment.
Give this skill's named section precedence over conflicting
`## conventions` rules. Use other relevant sections - by name match,
by topic (routing,
verification, worktrees, etc.), or by workflow convention - to override or
extend the instructions above. Project-local `AGENTS.md` is already in
context - check it for project-specific routing tables, service paths, and
verification commands.

The recognized headings, their readers, and the rules an override cannot change are listed in the [configuration front door](../../README.md#project-specific-overrides); an override extends or replaces the step it names and never lifts this skill's HARD CONSTRAINT or MUST text.

# Handoff brief contract (gauntlet-resume + gauntlet-handoff supplementary)

Consumed by `gauntlet-resume/SKILL.md` (consumer) and `gauntlet-handoff/SKILL.md`
(producer). Brief grammar lives only here; both skills cite this file and inline none of it
(`scripts/ci.mjs` drift lint). The six headings before `## Process state` and the
`## Repo state` fields are pi-cohort's `handoff` skill's; cohort drift is reconciled
here and nowhere else.

## Brief grammar

Headings, fixed order. A consumer keys on headings, never prose.

```markdown
# Handoff: <one line>
## Intent
## Repo state
## Decisions
## Open questions
## Skills loaded
## Process state
```

| Section | Content | Presence |
|---|---|---|
| `## Repo state` | one field per line: `toplevel`, `worktree: yes <path>` or `worktree: no`, `branch` (`detached` when none), `HEAD`, `base` (`unknown` when no remote resolves), `dirty: <porcelain>` or `dirty: clean`, `diff-stat` (`unavailable` when base unknown), `test cmd`; any field `unavailable` when its command failed; heading `## Repo state: not a git repo` outside git | always |
| `## Decisions` | bullets; rejected alternatives marked `rejected:` | always |
| `## Skills loaded` | frontmatter `name`s; `## Skills loaded: none` when none | always |
| `## Process state` | `phase_tracker status` then `plan_tracker status` verbatim; `Active task: <name|none>`; optional one or more consecutive `PR: <owner/repo#N>` / `Pre-rework head: <40-char sha>` pairs, one per record group, home first, in record order, only for a PR subject; optional single `Rework base: <40-char sha>` after all PR pairs; for more than one member only, the coordinated block from `coordinated.md` after that line; the line `Gate history not restored - re-validate before advancing.` | only when a phase is `in_progress` and no hotfix flow is in context |

For a loop ledger (line 1 exactly `# Ledger - loop engine`), replace `Active task` with these two fields, retaining both tracker status outputs and the gate-history line:

```text
Ledger: <path>
Last decision: <line>
```

Use the ledger path relative to the worktree and the last physical decision line, or `none` for an empty Decisions section. Read the ledger on disk; the brief is a pointer, not a second ledger state carrier. Permit task rows beside a ledger: copy `plan_tracker status` verbatim, including the dispatched row's `in_progress` status and any conformance tasks with their observed statuses. Never infer task state from the brief's prose. Reject a block mixing these fields with `Active task` or missing either loop field.

Consumer rules: process state absent -> plain handoff (the consumer starts its
own process from `## Intent`). Give valid ledger fields precedence over `No plan active.` and run ledger admission (`restore-loop.md`). Restore phase-only state for `No plan active.` only with no `Ledger` field. Load named skills as the consumer.

A brief is any text whose first line starts `# Handoff:` - a file on disk or pasted
inline. `## Repo state` is matched by prefix: `## Repo state` or
`## Repo state: not a git repo`.

## Producers

`gauntlet-handoff` is the only writer of `## Process state`; it appends to the file
cohort's `handoff` skill wrote, which ends at `## Skills loaded`. Drop exactly the last
line of the `phase_tracker status` output when it starts with `Context: `; copy the
rest verbatim. Layout, byte-exact: one blank line, the heading on its own line, a
blank line, that phase status, a blank line, the `plan_tracker status` output
verbatim, a blank line,
`Active task: <name|none>`, then, only for a PR subject, one or more consecutive
`PR: <owner/repo#N>` / `Pre-rework head: <40-char sha>` pairs, one per record group,
home first, in record order, then optional single `Rework base: <40-char sha>` after all PR pairs, then, for more than one member only, the coordinated block from `coordinated.md`, then the gate-history line after the last pair, rework-base line, or block -
unfenced, nothing after.
For a task plan, set `Active task` to the first `→` task name, else `none` (also for `No plan active.`). For a line-1 ledger, read its path and last decision and use the loop alternative above, retaining the optional PR pairs and rework base before the gate-history line. Copy the full rework base only from the top-level record when present; never invent a boundary for incomplete sync. Copy only top-level record pairs, without titles; `Threads:` and record `### PR #<N>` subsections are not brief fields. For N=1 emit one pair; without a Rework record use the ordinary layout.

Example appended block (the fence is documentation; the brief carries no fence):

```text

## Process state

Phases:
  ⊘ brainstorm (resume: <spec path>)
  ⊘ plan (resume: pasted brief)
  → implement(W2)
  ○ verify
  ○ ship

Plan: 1/3 done (1 in progress, 1 pending)

  ✓ [0] W1: contract
  → [1] W2: producer
  ○ [2] W2: consumer

Active task: W2: producer
Gate history not restored - re-validate before advancing.
```

## Tracker output grammar

Must match `formatStatus` in the phase-tracker and plan-tracker extensions.

```
Phases:
  ✓ brainstorm
  → implement(W2)
  ○ verify (reason)
```

Glyphs `✓` complete, `→` in_progress, `⊘` skipped, `○` pending; `(reason)` suffix when
set; `name(substep)` only on the in-progress phase.

```
Plan: 2/5 done (1 in progress, 2 pending)

  ✓ [0] <name>
  → [1] <name>
```

or `No plan active.`. Task glyphs `✓` complete, `→` in_progress, `✗` failed, `⊘` skipped,
`○` pending, mapping 1:1 onto `plan_tracker init` `{name, status}` statuses.

A ledger task row is `row <n>` plus a ` | <description>` display suffix (`restore-loop.md`).

Parse stops (print the offending line, make no tracker call):

- a task line not matching `^\s*[✓→✗⊘○] \[\d+\] .+$` - the "unparsable process-state
  task line" stop;
- a process-state section whose phase block shows all `○` - contradictory (the producer
  emits the section only with an in-progress phase);
- a phase block with more than one `→` line - contradictory (the tracker holds one active
  phase; print both lines).

name: loop-implementation
description: Use after approval selects the loop engine, or when resuming an acceptance-criteria ledger in the implement phase.
---

# Loop implementation

Run this driver in the main session. Carry the absolute implementation worktree path as a value; run git with `git -C "<worktree>"` and commands as `(cd "<worktree>" && <command>)`. Carry the approved spec path and resolved plan directory. Keep the original prompt for verify. Never run reviewers inside implement. Use `plan_tracker({ action: "refresh", path: <absolute ledger path> })` for every refresh; pass only the path and let the extension derive the view. After every admitted ledger commit (child or parent), refresh once; the seed refresh follows implement start below. Read [commit-message.md](../finishing-a-development-branch/reference/commit-message.md) for all commit wording. Resolve its absolute path from this loaded skill and resolve the ticket once at seed or authorized restore; pass `wording: <absolute path>` and `ticket: <reference or none>` to every worker. Use its fixed bookkeeping sentence for each parent event and its amendment source for amendments.

## Entry

1. Read project overrides below. Resolve `gauntlet_setting({ key: "loopEngine" })` and retain `maxIterationsPerRow` (default 4) and `escalateAfter` (default 3). Hold `escalateAfter` in driver memory for this run; never print it or write it to the ledger, and never re-resolve it inside the loop, including after amendment grant re-decodes. Stop on an unavailable settings tool. Select this run's seed value in step 4 and persist it only in the ledger, not in the spec or settings.
2. Resolve verification once using this ordered table. Print `verification command: <command> (<source>)`.

| Observed configuration | Action |
|---|---|
| Overrides `## PR gate` contains `- verification command:` | Use that command; source PR gate. |
| Otherwise overrides has `## verification-before-completion` | Use its exactly one backticked command; zero or several is a configuration error. |
| Neither section supplies a command | Discover the project's test entrypoint from its actual manifest/build instructions; print discovery as source. Stop on an unresolved or ambiguous entrypoint. |

At seed and at an authorized restore, before entering the dispatch loop, read the spec in full. Decode `**Amend-grant:**` through [amendment-surface Value decoding](../brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md). Capture the decoded grant, row dispositions, ordered leg membership, each leg's absolute checkout paths and combined spec/task Rules for dispatch and handoff; use home for zero or one leg. At an authorized fresh-session restore, resolve `gauntlet_setting({ key: "loopEngine" })` exactly once at this boundary and hold `escalateAfter` for the run; share that read with gauntlet-resume's `reference/restore-loop.md`. With an unavailable tool, stop before dispatch with `cannot resolve escalation threshold: settings tool unavailable (loopEngine.escalateAfter)`; never supply an in-loop default.

At seed and at an authorized restore, when the held membership has more than one leg, read `reference/coordinated-legs.md` IN FULL now with read at its absolute path; stop on an unreadable reference naming its path, never reconstruct it. On fresh entry apply its `## Entry` section at step 4 instead of the home-only skeleton below, using step 4's resolved allowance seed value. On a restore apply its `## Resume` section before the dirty-tree stop and before any pending recovery. Keep legacy and single-member ledger bytes unchanged, with no coordinated metadata.

3. Call `phase_tracker({ action: "skip", phase: "plan", reason: "loop engine" })`.
4. Require a clean named-branch implementation worktree. With dirty status and no `pending:` tuple, take ## Human stop before writing the ledger. Read the literal `run allowance: <n>` line from the invoking approval turn: it carries the approved `--allowance=N` flag's value. Use that value over step 1's setting; with no carrier use `maxIterationsPerRow`. Print `allowance: <n> (reply)` or `allowance: <n> (setting)` with the seeded header. Ignore the carrier once a ledger exists; resume uses its header only. Write `<resolved plan dir>/<spec stem>-ledger.md`. Use this grammar with literal values, not placeholders:

```markdown
# Ledger - loop engine
**Spec:** `doc/specs/example.md`
base: <HEAD SHA before skeleton>
verification: <resolved command>
checks: commands
iterations: 0
allowance: <n>
returned: none

| row | status | attempts | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | open | 0 | |

## Decisions
```

Use the actual repo-relative spec path alone in the Spec header. Read base with `git -C "<worktree>" rev-parse HEAD`. Index every spec AC in order, including nested disposition lines without treating them as extra ACs; keep row text only in the spec. Initialize explicit/absent `in-scope` and `venue:` rows `open`, attempts 0, evidence empty. Initialize only `deviates:`, `deferred:`, `elsewhere:` rows `cut`, attempts 0, disposition text as evidence. Write `allowance:` immediately after `iterations: 0` using step 4's seed value; never scale it by row count or seed dispatches: 24 non-cut rows at default 4 yield allowance 4. All-cut ledgers keep the same allowance and exit through rule 1 without a seed dispatch. Later cuts, reopens and requirement-preserving amendments leave allowance unchanged; redraw deletes the ledger and reseeds it. Serialize evidence in one physical table cell, result lines separated by semicolons, pipes escaped, plain text without angle markup.
5. Call `plan_check({ planPath: <ledger path> })`. Stop with findings as a configuration error. Commit the stamped skeleton with the shared Ledger skeleton sentence; call `phase_tracker({ action: "start", phase: "implement" })`, then `plan_tracker({ action: "refresh", path: <absolute ledger path> })`, including all-cut ledgers with no seed dispatch.

For resume, use the admitted ledger, its base and verification command, and durable iterations and allowance instead of overwriting it. Skip Entry step 1's allowance seeding for an admitted ledger; the allowance setting applies only to fresh seeding, and the restore boundary resolves `escalateAfter` once. Apply `/skill:gauntlet-resume` pending recovery before refresh and any unresolved dirty-tree stop. Render rows, allowance and decision history; route a recovered pending tuple through resume's pending recovery and ## Interrupted recovery before any unresolved dirty-tree stop.

## Driver holds

After seeding, restrict driver reads during implement to the ledger (including saved or committed ledger snapshots), the child's return file (one file reference), git boundary commands (`status --porcelain`, `rev-list --count`, `rev-parse`, `log -G'^returned: ' --format=%H <base>..HEAD -- <ledger path>`, ledger snapshots via `git show <sha>:<ledger path>`, and `rev-list --reverse --ancestry-path <S>..HEAD` plus `show --format= --name-only <worker sha>` in the tuple's owning checkout), the child's jobs file, OS process start identity and command, `ps -o pgid= -p <pid>`, `kill`, skill resources at their absolute paths and the overrides file. Keep rows by status, iterations, allowance, the last decision, the decoded amendment grant and each leg's checkout path for dispatch, handoff and stops. Use Entry's captured grant, row dispositions and membership throughout the loop.

Never read the spec, source files, test output or logs inside the implement loop. Never diagnose a failure's cause; carry the child's evidence into the next dispatch or human stop. Inside the implement loop, end a turn only with a stop header from ## Human stop; follow every intermediate report with the next ordered-table action in the same turn. The only log-read exception is the last 20 lines at the human stop in After the loop step 1. Leave spec reads for seed, authorized restore and the amendment action below, outside the loop.

## Before each dispatch

When the held membership has more than one leg, read `reference/coordinated-legs.md` IN FULL now with read at its absolute path; stop on an unreadable reference naming its path, never reconstruct it. Apply its `## Resume`, `## Targeting and dispatch`, `## Companion return validation`, `### Companion commit admission` and `## Amendments` sections together with this driver; never apply `## Entry` here.

Read the ledger and require its `checks:` line per ## Gate set.

Require exactly one `returned:` line before each dispatch; without one stop with `ledger has no returned: line - unsupported ledger format; finish this run on the pi-gauntlet release that wrote it`. Read the ledger and require `allowance:` and no `cap:` before the ordered table, including for seed and completed ledgers; otherwise stop with `ledger has no allowance: line - unsupported ledger format; finish this run on the pi-gauntlet release that wrote it`. Follow either stop with `recovery: doc/configuration.md "Loop engine operations"`. Keep `iterations:` as a dispatch counter only; it bounds nothing. Start each row's window after the later of its latest `row <n> retry` decision and the latest `amended` decision; with neither, start at ledger base. Never reach back past a returns conversion commit. An admitted amendment starts new windows for every row; raising allowance resets neither. Count consecutive validation misses from the window's child `row <n> done|failed` decisions and `repair row <n>` lines excluding those whose second cell starts `interrupted - `: the last two must both be repairs. Recover empty-child windows from ledger snapshots as below, never commit messages. Preserve every row's attempts and spent escalation. Before the ordered table, route each admitted failed target through ## Unreachable returns once at admission (including companions), or on resume when admitted but not yet routed; follow that reference's answered-stop rule after human decisions. Apply this ordered table, starting here after each return or human decision:

| Order | Observed state | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | No `open` or `failed` row | Refresh; require implement complete; continue at ## After the loop step 0. All-cut and baseline-complete ledgers exit here. |
| 2 | Unresolved row attempts >= effective allowance | Human stop with or without amend permission. Exempt `done` and `cut`. |
| 3 | Last two child row commits for the same row changed no file outside the ledger and no row status, or two consecutive validation misses on that row | Set the hint for that row: `the last two attempts changed nothing outside the ledger` for empty-child stagnation, or `two returns broke the contract: <concrete miss from the last repair evidence>` for validation misses; continue to rule 4. |
| 4 | Dispatch allowed | Select target by the priority below, then apply the escalation threshold check. |

Read [empty-child stagnation](./reference/empty-child-stagnation.md) at its absolute path now; stop if unreadable.

When a refresh leaves implement active at rule 1, take the matching human stop; never start verify. Before evaluating rule 2, compute each row's effective allowance as the ledger's `allowance:` plus the count of that row's `row <n> retry | ... | allowed attempts <m>` lines in `## Decisions`. Count each retry once; the stored `<m>` is historical, not an absolute override. Ignore every other decision and grant in this arithmetic. Use the same rule for every coordinated entry, regardless of leg. With allowance 4 and two retries, a row has effective allowance 6 even if the historical `<m>` values are 5 and 99; raising the shared header to 7 makes it 9, while an unretried row gets 7. A row already at or above its effective allowance is exhausted. Never reset or reduce attempts.

Use the held decoded amendment grant for amendment choices only; ignore its waves-only budget token, retaining no amend permission for a budget-only value. Never consult this value for row escalation. Apply rule 2 before rule 3; a rule-3 hint dispatches through rule 4. Preserve `STAGNANT`, `REJECT` and closureReview boundaries; After the loop step 3 funds conformance rounds from the allowance.

Select `seed` until the ledger at HEAD holds an admitted `row 0 done | seeded ...` decision, independently of `iterations`; before any seed dispatch apply ## Validate the return's seed count instead of rule 3's row windows. Otherwise select the still-unresolved human retry target, then the still-failed row named by the previous decision, then first failed row, then first open row. Read seed completion from the ledger at HEAD, never commit messages or evidence completeness. Never re-seed a validated partial seed to fill empty evidence cells. Use the latest admitted return's target decision for targeting and the child's `previous decision:` input, never an extra's line; skip allowance-grant and legacy grant history while retaining the entire Decisions section. Durable status beats a decision's suggestion. Keep the retry hint only for its target.

For a numbered target with no durable `row <n> escalated` decision, compute `threshold = min(escalateAfter, effective allowance - 1)` from the held `escalateAfter` and the row's effective allowance. When the row's pre-dispatch attempts >= threshold, make this dispatch the escalated round: resolve `gauntlet_setting({ key: "escalationLoop" })` with or without amend permission. Use the returned non-empty `implModel` string, including the resolver's main-loop model fallback when the setting is unset or malformed. With the settings tool unavailable or `implModel` undefined (neither a configured model nor a main-loop model), stop before dispatch with `Problem: escalationLoop.implModel unavailable`; write no escalation decision and leave attempts unchanged. Never substitute a default-model attempt for that stop.

With the resolved model, append `row <n> escalated | implModel round | allowed attempts <effective allowance>`, commit with the shared Escalation sentence, print `escalated round for row <n>`, and dispatch that attempt with `model: <implModel>` through the normal loop-implementer target, bump and validation path. Exclude this parent commit from child-only stagnation; it starts no new empty-child or validation-miss window. With defaults (allowance 4, `escalateAfter` 3), escalate attempt 4; clamp larger thresholds to the last allowed attempt. At allowance 1, escalate the first and only allowed attempt. A row found past the threshold unspent escalates on its next dispatch. Treat the escalated decision as exactly one round within the effective allowance, never an extra attempt. Recover the row's escalation identity from `## Decisions` on every dispatch and resume; unrecoverable means spent. Preserve `row <n> escalated` for the whole flow across retry, `rows +N`, amendments and resume. Once spent, omit the model override on every later authorized attempt, including every attempt up to a raised effective allowance; never resolve another row escalation or append a second marker. With no marker and recoverable history, apply the threshold predicate after retry or `rows +N`; a previously missing model or migrated row has not spent escalation. Dispatch errors, non-DONE and validation failures consume it before any recommendation decision.

## Dispatch

For home dispatch, record `HEAD_BEFORE`, save the ledger before the iterations bump and tuple write, and retain the current `iterations:` count as i. Send `iteration: i` using the current pre-bump `iterations:` count and write `iterations: i + 1` before dispatch; admission requires the committed ledger's `iterations:` to carry `i + 1`. State that difference when rendering a dispatch or admission: the task carries the pre-bump count, while the ledger and an outside-ledger return's `iteration:` carry the consumed count; never compare them to the task's count. Record the dispatch identity separately and write `pending: <row or seed> | <repo> | <HEAD sha>` using `home` for zero or one spec leg, the actual member identifier for coordinated runs, and the selected checkout's HEAD. Persist the consumed count and tuple before every home or companion dispatch; then refresh. Commit nothing extra. Create a unique absolute output path with `mktemp` outside the repository. Dispatch exactly one foreground child in the main implementation worktree, not a nested worktree:

```text
subagent({ agent: "loop-implementer", context: "fresh", async: false,
  cwd: <absolute implementation worktree>, output: <unique absolute temp path>,
  outputMode: "file-only",
  acceptance: { level: "none", reason: "the parent validates the ledger and the commit" },
  task: "iteration: <i>\nspec: <absolute spec path>\nledger: <absolute ledger path>\nbase: <base SHA>\ntarget: <row number or seed>\nprevious decision: <new conforming line or none>\nhint: <human hint or none>\nwording: <absolute path>\nticket: <reference or none>" })
```

For `target: seed`, explicitly instruct the child to apply its seed contract even when iteration is greater than 0; carry that instruction in the existing `hint` field. Keep the actual consumed pre-bump count in `iteration`.

Omit the model override except on an escalated round (`model: <implModel>`); let the persona override or parent inheritance resolve it. Carry effects only: one file-reference return, one ledger read, git boundary checks. Never read a child transcript or carry reasoning history. Route a dispatch error (including `Request aborted` or any tool-reported `error: <text>`, even with an empty return file) or non-DONE return, including a silence kill, through ## Interrupted recovery. An async handle still stops; never poll or join it. Redispatch only through the ordered table after completed recovery.

## Validate the return

For home returns, apply the following boundary and table. Never project terminal child results before clean/exactly-one-commit admission.
1. Require a DONE return, empty `git -C "<worktree>" status --porcelain` and exactly 1 from `git -C "<worktree>" rev-list HEAD_BEFORE..HEAD --count`. Require the ledger at HEAD to carry the dispatched tuple as its `returned:` value or on a retained `pending:` line, and `iterations:` equal to saved +1. A tuple on neither line is wrong attribution; a retained tuple remains a result-validation miss. Route dispatch errors, non-DONE, killed, dirty, zero/multiple-commit and wrong-attribution returns through ## Interrupted recovery, not result admission. Read result rows and decisions from the ledger at HEAD only after this boundary passes.
2. Validate by dispatched `target`, not iteration number, against the saved copy using this table. Admit exactly three header changes: `iterations` +1, removal of the dispatched `pending:` line and replacement of `returned:` with the dispatched tuple's value; reject every other header change, including allowance. Preserve row identifiers and prior decisions.

| Target | Required changes | Miss |
|---|---|---|
| Seed | Require bounded nonempty evidence on at least one non-cut row; admit a subset or all rows. All attempts stay 0; only `open` -> `done` status transitions; keep unreached rows unchanged, including open rows with empty evidence, and preserve cut rows. Require exactly one new `row 0 done | seeded <k> rows, closed <m> on baseline | <first row to take>` decision, counting only rows given evidence in this return and their proven baseline closures. Partial and complete baseline closure both pass. Never `failed`. | Seed repair below; redispatch seed while its repair count is below allowance. |
| Ordinary | Require the target row's mutable cells to change: status `done` or `failed`, attempts +1, nonempty bounded evidence. Admit zero or more other rows in the same leg changing `open` -> `done`, each with nonempty bounded evidence and attempts unchanged. Require set equality between changed rows and rows with exactly one new decision line, target first, each matching its row and status. Keep every other row, header and prior decision unchanged apart from the dispatch header changes in step 2. | Parent repair below. |
| Seed or ordinary | No committed `pending:` tuple remains. | A retained committed tuple is a validation miss for the dispatched target after boundary admission, not a boundary rejection. |

Require each ordinary decision to match `^row <that row> <that status> \| .{1,200} \| .{1,200}$`; an old conforming line is not a new line. Require check name plus at most three result lines in evidence, serialized with semicolons and escaped pipes as in the persona; add no command-format check. Reject a `failed` extra, a foreign-leg extra, a changed `cut` or `done` row, extra attempts changes, empty evidence on a changed row, or a missing, duplicate, malformed or unmatched decision. Admit an evidenced `done` extra beside a `failed` target. Never police worker ordering or execute a check after a return; leave regressions to verify step 1's gate set. Declare extras only in the ledger diff and their decision lines; inspect no commit message.

On a seed miss after clean/exactly-one-commit admission, restore every non-cut row, headers (including the saved allowance) and decisions from the saved copy; preserve cut rows and retain the incremented iterations. Clear `pending:` and retain the dispatched tuple in `returned:`, setting it when the child retained pending. Append `repair seed | seed miss: <concrete miss> | iteration <consumed>` and commit with the shared Seed repair sentence, then refresh and apply the seed count below. A validated seed resets the validation-miss window, so ordinary dispatch starts clean. Exclude seed repairs from rule 3's row windows.

Count seed attempts as `repair seed` lines in the home ledger, including interrupted and validation-miss repairs; never count commit messages. Dispatch seed while this count is below the ledger allowance, with the seed-contract instruction and `seed miss: <concrete miss>` or `seed interrupted: <reason>` in `hint:`, and `previous decision: none`. Recover the count and reason from those decision lines on resume, using the latest repair's second cell as the hint. At allowance render `Stopped on seed` with `seed: <k> of <allowance>` and the retry/`rows +N` menu; only a raised allowance permits more seed repairs, and a numbered retry never erases this count. Keep row attempts at 0.

On an ordinary miss restore every non-target row, headers (including the saved allowance) and prior decisions from the saved copy, retaining the incremented iterations. Set the target `failed`, attempts = saved attempts +1, evidence = `iteration <i>: <concrete miss>`. Clear `pending:`, keep or set `returned:` to the dispatched tuple, remove malformed appended decisions and append `repair row <n> | <concrete miss> | iteration <consumed>`. Commit with the shared Row repair sentence, then refresh. Set previous decision to `none`; on an admitted ordinary return use the target's new conforming line, never the last extra's. Two consecutive validation misses on a row set its rule-3 hint. A conforming return resets the consecutive-miss count; parent repair commits do not count toward child-only empty stagnation.

## Unreachable returns

Read [unreachable-returns](reference/unreachable-returns.md) in full now with read at its absolute path; apply its evidence routing before returning to the ordered table.

## Interrupted recovery

Read [interrupted recovery](reference/interrupted-recovery.md) in full now; apply its numbered procedure before redispatch.

Read and apply [menu-layout](../brainstorming/reference/menu-layout.md). Put it alone on the first output line, followed by a newline before the stop text, without a driver-state preamble, wrapper or code fence. These decisions are neither done nor stuck outcomes.

| Human choice | Durable action |

Commit both changes exactly once using the shared Allowance raise sentence, leaving iterations and all attempts unchanged; return to the ordered table. Keep single-member/legacy paths free of a companion loop, leg file, `legs:` brief or `--leg` argument.

0. Call `phase_tracker({ action: "start", phase: "verify" })`. Mint `LOG_DIR=$(mktemp -d)` once for this verify session; a resumed session mints a new one at its first gate-set site.

Any repair invalidates that run: apply the rerun scope below before the next gate. No task reopen/update is awaited.
   Count `repairs` as `repair verification` lines in the home ledger plus one for a `pending: verify` tuple on disk. Use the shared ledger allowance, with no per-row retry increments.    On failure automatically repair while `repairs < allowance` with or without amend permission; never consult amend permission or gate on iterations. Keep verify active and implement complete. Treat only that bump/tuple as expected home dirt. Dispatch exactly one `implementer` with `model: <implModel>`, `context: "fresh"`, `async: false`, failing checkout cwd and Rules, absolute spec path, failing command, checkout, exit code and log path, never pasted output. Pass the exact pending tuple and consumed `iteration:`, the held `wording:` and `ticket:`, plus the failing leg's base and pre-bump iteration for jobs-file identity. Require a shared-wording repair message with no dispatch state. For a companion repair, prepare a return path through coordinated-legs' Return file section and pass `return:`; require only the tuple and consumed iteration on its first two lines, with no rows or decisions. Inject the persona's step-5 action authorization without its row mutation protocol. Include this blocking-call contract in the repair task: bound every blocking command with `timeout -k 30 <n>`, n <= 600; background and poll longer work. Read [loop-implementer's Evidence command](../../agents/loop-implementer.md#evidence-command) and copy its first three paragraphs verbatim into that task, omitting its row/seed ledger protocol. The repair child reads the log to derive the files to touch; for a stale selector restore the test or its name, never ledger evidence.
   Require DONE, a clean failing checkout and exactly one commit after HEAD_BEFORE. For home attribution require the committed ledger's consumed `iterations:` and retained `pending: verify` tuple; for a companion require that attribution on the return file's first two lines with nothing after them, unchanged home HEAD and only expected bump/tuple dirt. Require all ledger rows, attempts, mapping, allowance, `returned:` and prior decisions unchanged. A clean commit with wrong attribution or any protected-state change takes the interrupted path below. Commit with the shared Verification repair marker sentence, delete the companion return file and refresh. After that rerun passes, run the original fail-fast run's still-unexecuted pairs from other checkouts in ledger order before recording verified HEAD. On resume run the complete gate set in a fresh session LOG_DIR. A new failure in any leg returns to the repair-count check; do not reopen rows or reset the count. Never spend verify-phase credits. 2. Dispatch foreground whole-diff `wave-reviewer` per `/skill:requesting-code-review`, from ledger base through committed HEAD, with `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: none`. Apply its fix rounds. Follow the reference's partition, concern decomposition, fix rounds and Convergence with the gate set replacing plan Verification at every test site per the reference's ledger-subject override.    When the conformance fix-round cap blocks (`<used> fix round(s) used against a cap of <cap>`) or the reference's step 6 asks at its cap, read `<used>` from that text. Leave the cap and settings unchanged.
   On an approved re-bound (`reopened by amendment`), use the held grant. Without amend permission, refresh and stop with `Stopped: row <n> reopened by amendment during verify`; offer authorize the row's return to ledger implementation or stop. Under amend permission, continue without a second authorization. Emit exact `## Closure / conformance` schema from the reference: `status: CONFORMS (0 open)` or `status: GAPS (N open)`, then `audited-base: <full HEAD SHA>`, happy-path exactly when run, Deferred/deviates per spec exactly when applicable, all gap/concern fields unchanged, auto-applied fix commits index and whole-diff minors. ## Project overrides

If a gauntlet overrides file exists - checked in order: `.pi/gauntlet-overrides.md`, `<repo root>/gauntlet-overrides.md`, `<repo root>/doc/gauntlet-overrides.md`; first found wins - read it once per session - a skill that already has the file's content in context from an earlier skill's read skips the read; a restored session has nothing in context and reads it. Read and apply `## conventions` whenever present, without a relevance judgment. Give this skill's named section precedence over conflicting `## conventions` rules. Use other relevant sections - by name match, by topic (routing, verification, worktrees, etc.), or by workflow convention - to override or extend the instructions above. Project-local `AGENTS.md` is already in context - check it for project-specific routing tables, service paths, and verification commands.

The recognized headings, their readers, and the rules an override cannot change are listed in the [configuration front door](../../README.md#project-specific-overrides); an override extends or replaces the step it names and never lifts this skill's HARD CONSTRAINT or MUST text.

# Loop implementation

Run this driver in the main session. Carry the absolute implementation worktree path as a value; run git with `git -C "<worktree>"` and commands as `(cd "<worktree>" && <command>)`. Carry the approved spec path and resolved plan directory. Keep the original prompt for verify. Never run reviewers inside implement. Use `plan_tracker({ action: "refresh", path: <absolute ledger path> })` for every refresh; pass only the path and let the extension derive the view. After every admitted ledger commit (child or parent), refresh once; the seed refresh follows implement start below. Read [commit-message.md](../finishing-a-development-branch/reference/commit-message.md) for all commit wording. Resolve its absolute path from this loaded skill and resolve the ticket once at seed or authorized restore; pass `wording: <absolute path>` and `ticket: <reference or none>` to every worker. Use its fixed bookkeeping sentence for each parent event and its amendment source for amendments.

## Entry

1. Read project overrides below. Resolve `gauntlet_setting({ key: "loopEngine" })` and retain `maxIterationsPerRow` (default 4) and `escalateAfter` (default 3). Hold `escalateAfter` in driver memory for this run; never print it or write it to the ledger, and never re-resolve it inside the loop, including after amendment grant re-decodes. Stop on an unavailable settings tool. Select this run's seed value in step 4 and persist it only in the ledger, not in the spec or settings.
2. Resolve verification once using this ordered table. Print `verification command: <command> (<source>)`.

| Observed configuration | Action |
|---|---|
| Overrides `## PR gate` contains `- verification command:` | Use that command; source PR gate. |
| Otherwise overrides has `## verification-before-completion` | Use its exactly one backticked command; zero or several is a configuration error. |
| Neither section supplies a command | Discover the project's test entrypoint from its actual manifest/build instructions; print discovery as source. Stop on an unresolved or ambiguous entrypoint. |

At seed and at an authorized restore, before entering the dispatch loop, read the spec in full. Decode `**Amend-grant:**` through [amendment-surface Value decoding](../brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md). Capture the decoded grant, row dispositions, ordered leg membership, each leg's absolute checkout paths and combined spec/task Rules for dispatch and handoff; use home for zero or one leg. At an authorized fresh-session restore, resolve `gauntlet_setting({ key: "loopEngine" })` exactly once at this boundary and hold `escalateAfter` for the run; share that read with gauntlet-resume's `reference/restore-loop.md`. With an unavailable tool, stop before dispatch with `cannot resolve escalation threshold: settings tool unavailable (loopEngine.escalateAfter)`; never supply an in-loop default.

At seed and at an authorized restore, when the held membership has more than one leg, read `reference/coordinated-legs.md` IN FULL now with read at its absolute path; stop on an unreadable reference naming its path, never reconstruct it. 3. Call `phase_tracker({ action: "skip", phase: "plan", reason: "loop engine" })`.
4. Require a clean named-branch implementation worktree. With dirty status and no `pending:` tuple, take ## Human stop before writing the ledger. Ignore the carrier once a ledger exists; resume uses its header only. Write `<resolved plan dir>/<spec stem>-ledger.md`. Use this grammar with literal values, not placeholders:

```markdown
# Ledger - loop engine
**Spec:** `doc/specs/example.md`
base: <HEAD SHA before skeleton>
verification: <resolved command>
checks: commands
iterations: 0
allowance: <n>
returned: none

| row | status | attempts | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | open | 0 | |

Use the actual repo-relative spec path alone in the Spec header. Read base with `git -C "<worktree>" rev-parse HEAD`. Index every spec AC in order, including nested disposition lines without treating them as extra ACs; keep row text only in the spec. Initialize explicit/absent `in-scope` and `venue:` rows `open`, attempts 0, evidence empty. Initialize only `deviates:`, `deferred:`, `elsewhere:` rows `cut`, attempts 0, disposition text as evidence. Skip Entry step 1's allowance seeding for an admitted ledger; the allowance setting applies only to fresh seeding, and the restore boundary resolves `escalateAfter` once. Apply `/skill:gauntlet-resume` pending recovery before refresh and any unresolved dirty-tree stop. Render rows, allowance and decision history; route a recovered pending tuple through resume's pending recovery and ## Interrupted recovery before any unresolved dirty-tree stop.

## Driver holds

## Before each dispatch

Before the ordered table, route each admitted failed target through ## Unreachable returns once at admission (including companions), or on resume when admitted but not yet routed; follow that reference's answered-stop rule after human decisions. Apply this ordered table, starting here after each return or human decision:

On an ordinary miss restore every non-target row, headers (including the saved allowance) and prior decisions from the saved copy, retaining the incremented iterations. 5. Immediately invoke `/skill:finishing-a-development-branch <abs worktree path>`. Its menu is the human gate; do not add a ready-to-finish prompt.

## Project overrides

If a gauntlet overrides file exists - checked in order: `.pi/gauntlet-overrides.md`, `<repo root>/gauntlet-overrides.md`, `<repo root>/doc/gauntlet-overrides.md`; first found wins - read it once per session - a skill that already has the file's content in context from an earlier skill's read skips the read; a restored session has nothing in context and reads it. Read and apply `## conventions` whenever present, without a relevance judgment. Give this skill's named section precedence over conflicting `## conventions` rules. Use other relevant sections - by name match, by topic (routing, verification, worktrees, etc.), or by workflow convention - to override or extend the instructions above. Project-local `AGENTS.md` is already in context - check it for project-specific routing tables, service paths, and verification commands.

The recognized headings, their readers, and the rules an override cannot change are listed in the [configuration front door](../../README.md#project-specific-overrides); an override extends or replaces the step it names and never lifts this skill's HARD CONSTRAINT or MUST text.
