---
name: loop-implementation
description: Use after approval selects the loop engine, or when resuming an acceptance-criteria ledger in the implement phase.
---

# Loop implementation

Run this driver in the main session. Carry the absolute implementation worktree path as a value; run git with `git -C "<worktree>"` and commands as `(cd "<worktree>" && <command>)`. Carry the approved spec path and resolved plan directory. Keep the original prompt for verify. Never run reviewers inside implement. Use `plan_tracker({ action: "refresh", path: <absolute ledger path> })` for every refresh; pass only the path and let the extension derive the view. After every admitted ledger commit (child or parent), refresh once; the seed refresh follows implement start below. Read [commit-message.md](../finishing-a-development-branch/reference/commit-message.md) for all commit wording. Resolve its absolute path from this loaded skill and resolve the ticket once at seed or authorized restore; pass `wording: <absolute path>` and `ticket: <reference or none>` to every worker. Use its fixed bookkeeping sentence for each parent event and its amendment source for amendments.

## Entry

1. Read project overrides below. Resolve `gauntlet_setting({ key: "loopEngine" })` and retain `maxIterationsPerRow` (default 4) and `escalateAfter` (default 3). Hold `escalateAfter` in driver memory for this run; never print it or write it to the ledger, and never re-resolve it inside the loop, including after amendment grant re-decodes. Stop on an unavailable settings tool. Select this run's seed value in step 4 and persist it only in the ledger, not in the spec or settings.
2. Resolve verification once using this ordered table. Print `verification command: <command> (<source>)`.

| Observed configuration | Action |
|---|---|
| Overrides `## PR gate` contains `- verification command:` | Use that command; source PR gate. |
| Otherwise overrides has `## verification-before-completion` | Use its exactly one backticked command; zero or several is a configuration error. |
| Neither section supplies a command | Discover the project's test entrypoint from its actual manifest/build instructions; print discovery as source. Stop on an unresolved or ambiguous entrypoint. |

At seed and at an authorized restore, before entering the dispatch loop, read the spec in full. Decode `**Amend-grant:**` through [amendment-surface Value decoding](../brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md). Capture the decoded grant, row dispositions, ordered leg membership, each leg's absolute checkout paths and combined spec/task Rules for dispatch and handoff; use home for zero or one leg. At an authorized fresh-session restore, resolve `gauntlet_setting({ key: "loopEngine" })` exactly once at this boundary and hold `escalateAfter` for the run; share that read with gauntlet-resume's `reference/restore-loop.md`. With an unavailable tool, stop before dispatch with `cannot resolve escalation threshold: settings tool unavailable (loopEngine.escalateAfter)`; never supply an in-loop default.

At seed and at an authorized restore, when the held membership has more than one leg, read `reference/coordinated-legs.md` IN FULL now with read at its absolute path; stop on an unreadable reference naming its path, never reconstruct it. On fresh entry apply its `## Entry` section at step 4 instead of the home-only skeleton below, using step 4's resolved allowance seed value. On a restore apply its `## Resume` section before the dirty-tree stop and before any pending recovery. Keep legacy and single-member ledger bytes unchanged, with no coordinated metadata.

3. Call `phase_tracker({ action: "skip", phase: "plan", reason: "loop engine" })`.
4. Require a clean named-branch implementation worktree. With dirty status and no `pending:` tuple, take ## Human stop before writing the ledger. Read the literal `run allowance: <n>` line from the invoking approval turn: it carries the approved `--allowance=N` flag's value. Use that value over step 1's setting; with no carrier use `maxIterationsPerRow`. Print `allowance: <n> (reply)` or `allowance: <n> (setting)` with the seeded header. Ignore the carrier once a ledger exists; resume uses its header only. Write `<resolved plan dir>/<spec stem>-ledger.md`. Use this grammar with literal values, not placeholders:

```markdown
# Ledger - loop engine
**Spec:** `doc/specs/example.md`
base: <HEAD SHA before skeleton>
verification: <resolved command>
checks: commands
iterations: 0
allowance: <n>
returned: none

| row | status | attempts | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | open | 0 | |

## Decisions
```

Use the actual repo-relative spec path alone in the Spec header. Read base with `git -C "<worktree>" rev-parse HEAD`. Index every spec AC in order, including nested disposition lines without treating them as extra ACs; keep row text only in the spec. Initialize explicit/absent `in-scope` and `venue:` rows `open`, attempts 0, evidence empty. Initialize only `deviates:`, `deferred:`, `elsewhere:` rows `cut`, attempts 0, disposition text as evidence. Write `allowance:` immediately after `iterations: 0` using step 4's seed value; never scale it by row count or seed dispatches: 24 non-cut rows at default 4 yield allowance 4. All-cut ledgers keep the same allowance and exit through rule 1 without a seed dispatch. Later cuts, reopens and requirement-preserving amendments leave allowance unchanged; redraw deletes the ledger and reseeds it. Serialize evidence in one physical table cell, result lines separated by semicolons, pipes escaped, plain text without angle markup.
5. Call `plan_check({ planPath: <ledger path> })`. Stop with findings as a configuration error. Commit the stamped skeleton with the shared Ledger skeleton sentence; call `phase_tracker({ action: "start", phase: "implement" })`, then `plan_tracker({ action: "refresh", path: <absolute ledger path> })`, including all-cut ledgers with no seed dispatch.

For resume, use the admitted ledger, its base and verification command, and durable iterations and allowance instead of overwriting it. Skip Entry step 1's allowance seeding for an admitted ledger; the allowance setting applies only to fresh seeding, and the restore boundary resolves `escalateAfter` once. Apply `/skill:gauntlet-resume` pending recovery before refresh and any unresolved dirty-tree stop. Render rows, allowance and decision history; route a recovered pending tuple through resume's pending recovery and ## Interrupted recovery before any unresolved dirty-tree stop.

## Driver holds

After seeding, restrict driver reads during implement to the ledger (including saved or committed ledger snapshots), the child's return file (one file reference), git boundary commands (`status --porcelain`, `rev-list --count`, `rev-parse`, `log -G'^returned: ' --format=%H <base>..HEAD -- <ledger path>`, ledger snapshots via `git show <sha>:<ledger path>`, and `rev-list --reverse --ancestry-path <S>..HEAD` plus `show --format= --name-only <worker sha>` in the tuple's owning checkout), the child's jobs file, OS process start identity and command, `ps -o pgid= -p <pid>`, `kill`, skill resources at their absolute paths and the overrides file. Keep rows by status, iterations, allowance, the last decision, the decoded amendment grant and each leg's checkout path for dispatch, handoff and stops. Use Entry's captured grant, row dispositions and membership throughout the loop.

Never read the spec, source files, test output or logs inside the implement loop. Never diagnose a failure's cause; carry the child's evidence into the next dispatch or human stop. Inside the implement loop, end a turn only with a stop header from ## Human stop; follow every intermediate report with the next ordered-table action in the same turn. The only log-read exception is the last 20 lines at the human stop in After the loop step 1. Leave spec reads for seed, authorized restore and the amendment action below, outside the loop.

## Before each dispatch

When the held membership has more than one leg, read `reference/coordinated-legs.md` IN FULL now with read at its absolute path; stop on an unreadable reference naming its path, never reconstruct it. Apply its `## Resume`, `## Targeting and dispatch`, `## Companion return validation`, `### Companion commit admission` and `## Amendments` sections together with this driver; never apply `## Entry` here.

Read the ledger and require its `checks:` line per ## Gate set.

Require exactly one `returned:` line before each dispatch; without one stop with `ledger has no returned: line - unsupported ledger format; finish this run on the pi-gauntlet release that wrote it`. Read the ledger and require `allowance:` and no `cap:` before the ordered table, including for seed and completed ledgers; otherwise stop with `ledger has no allowance: line - unsupported ledger format; finish this run on the pi-gauntlet release that wrote it`. Follow either stop with `recovery: doc/configuration.md "Loop engine operations"`. Keep `iterations:` as a dispatch counter only; it bounds nothing. Start each row's window after the later of its latest `row <n> retry` decision and the latest `amended` decision; with neither, start at ledger base. Never reach back past a returns conversion commit. An admitted amendment starts new windows for every row; raising allowance resets neither. Count consecutive validation misses from the window's child `row <n> done|failed` decisions and `repair row <n>` lines excluding those whose second cell starts `interrupted - `: the last two must both be repairs. Recover empty-child windows from ledger snapshots as below, never commit messages. Preserve every row's attempts and spent escalation. Before the ordered table, route each admitted failed target through ## Unreachable returns once at admission (including companions), or on resume when admitted but not yet routed; follow that reference's answered-stop rule after human decisions. Apply this ordered table, starting here after each return or human decision:

| Order | Observed state | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | No `open` or `failed` row | Refresh; require implement complete; continue at ## After the loop step 0. All-cut and baseline-complete ledgers exit here. |
| 2 | Unresolved row attempts >= effective allowance | Human stop with or without amend permission. Exempt `done` and `cut`. |
| 3 | Last two child row commits for the same row changed no file outside the ledger and no row status, or two consecutive validation misses on that row | Set the hint for that row: `the last two attempts changed nothing outside the ledger` for empty-child stagnation, or `two returns broke the contract: <concrete miss from the last repair evidence>` for validation misses; continue to rule 4. |
| 4 | Dispatch allowed | Select target by the priority below, then apply the escalation threshold check. |

Read [empty-child stagnation](./reference/empty-child-stagnation.md) at its absolute path now; stop if unreadable.

When a refresh leaves implement active at rule 1, take the matching human stop; never start verify. Before evaluating rule 2, compute each row's effective allowance as the ledger's `allowance:` plus the count of that row's `row <n> retry | ... | allowed attempts <m>` lines in `## Decisions`. Count each retry once; the stored `<m>` is historical, not an absolute override. Ignore every other decision and grant in this arithmetic. Use the same rule for every coordinated entry, regardless of leg. With allowance 4 and two retries, a row has effective allowance 6 even if the historical `<m>` values are 5 and 99; raising the shared header to 7 makes it 9, while an unretried row gets 7. A row already at or above its effective allowance is exhausted. Never reset or reduce attempts.

Use the held decoded amendment grant for amendment choices only; ignore its waves-only budget token, retaining no amend permission for a budget-only value. Never consult this value for row escalation. Apply rule 2 before rule 3; a rule-3 hint dispatches through rule 4. Preserve `STAGNANT`, `REJECT` and closureReview boundaries; After the loop step 3 funds conformance rounds from the allowance.

Select `seed` until the ledger at HEAD holds an admitted `row 0 done | seeded ...` decision, independently of `iterations`; before any seed dispatch apply ## Validate the return's seed count instead of rule 3's row windows. Otherwise select the still-unresolved human retry target, then the still-failed row named by the previous decision, then first failed row, then first open row. Read seed completion from the ledger at HEAD, never commit messages or evidence completeness. Never re-seed a validated partial seed to fill empty evidence cells. Use the latest admitted return's target decision for targeting and the child's `previous decision:` input, never an extra's line; skip allowance-grant and legacy grant history while retaining the entire Decisions section. Durable status beats a decision's suggestion. Keep the retry hint only for its target.

For a numbered target with no durable `row <n> escalated` decision, compute `threshold = min(escalateAfter, effective allowance - 1)` from the held `escalateAfter` and the row's effective allowance. When the row's pre-dispatch attempts >= threshold, make this dispatch the escalated round: resolve `gauntlet_setting({ key: "escalationLoop" })` with or without amend permission. Use the returned non-empty `implModel` string, including the resolver's main-loop model fallback when the setting is unset or malformed. With the settings tool unavailable or `implModel` undefined (neither a configured model nor a main-loop model), stop before dispatch with `Problem: escalationLoop.implModel unavailable`; write no escalation decision and leave attempts unchanged. Never substitute a default-model attempt for that stop.

With the resolved model, append `row <n> escalated | implModel round | allowed attempts <effective allowance>`, commit with the shared Escalation sentence, print `escalated round for row <n>`, and dispatch that attempt with `model: <implModel>` through the normal loop-implementer target, bump and validation path. Exclude this parent commit from child-only stagnation; it starts no new empty-child or validation-miss window. With defaults (allowance 4, `escalateAfter` 3), escalate attempt 4; clamp larger thresholds to the last allowed attempt. At allowance 1, escalate the first and only allowed attempt. A row found past the threshold unspent escalates on its next dispatch. Treat the escalated decision as exactly one round within the effective allowance, never an extra attempt. Recover the row's escalation identity from `## Decisions` on every dispatch and resume; unrecoverable means spent. Preserve `row <n> escalated` for the whole flow across retry, `rows +N`, amendments and resume. Once spent, omit the model override on every later authorized attempt, including every attempt up to a raised effective allowance; never resolve another row escalation or append a second marker. With no marker and recoverable history, apply the threshold predicate after retry or `rows +N`; a previously missing model or migrated row has not spent escalation. Dispatch errors, non-DONE and validation failures consume it before any recommendation decision.

## Dispatch

For home dispatch, record `HEAD_BEFORE`, save the ledger before the iterations bump and tuple write, and retain the current `iterations:` count as i. Send `iteration: i` using the current pre-bump `iterations:` count and write `iterations: i + 1` before dispatch; admission requires the committed ledger's `iterations:` to carry `i + 1`. State that difference when rendering a dispatch or admission: the task carries the pre-bump count, while the ledger and an outside-ledger return's `iteration:` carry the consumed count; never compare them to the task's count. Record the dispatch identity separately and write `pending: <row or seed> | <repo> | <HEAD sha>` using `home` for zero or one spec leg, the actual member identifier for coordinated runs, and the selected checkout's HEAD. Persist the consumed count and tuple before every home or companion dispatch; then refresh. Commit nothing extra. Create a unique absolute output path with `mktemp` outside the repository. Dispatch exactly one foreground child in the main implementation worktree, not a nested worktree:

```text
subagent({ agent: "loop-implementer", context: "fresh", async: false,
  cwd: <absolute implementation worktree>, output: <unique absolute temp path>,
  outputMode: "file-only",
  acceptance: { level: "none", reason: "the parent validates the ledger and the commit" },
  task: "iteration: <i>\nspec: <absolute spec path>\nledger: <absolute ledger path>\nbase: <base SHA>\ntarget: <row number or seed>\nprevious decision: <new conforming line or none>\nhint: <human hint or none>\nwording: <absolute path>\nticket: <reference or none>" })
```

For `target: seed`, explicitly instruct the child to apply its seed contract even when iteration is greater than 0; carry that instruction in the existing `hint` field. Keep the actual consumed pre-bump count in `iteration`.

Omit the model override except on an escalated round (`model: <implModel>`); let the persona override or parent inheritance resolve it. Carry effects only: one file-reference return, one ledger read, git boundary checks. Never read a child transcript or carry reasoning history. Route a dispatch error (including `Request aborted` or any tool-reported `error: <text>`, even with an empty return file) or non-DONE return, including a silence kill, through ## Interrupted recovery. An async handle still stops; never poll or join it. Redispatch only through the ordered table after completed recovery.

## Validate the return

For home returns, apply the following boundary and table. Never project terminal child results before clean/exactly-one-commit admission.
1. Require a DONE return, empty `git -C "<worktree>" status --porcelain` and exactly 1 from `git -C "<worktree>" rev-list HEAD_BEFORE..HEAD --count`. Require the ledger at HEAD to carry the dispatched tuple as its `returned:` value or on a retained `pending:` line, and `iterations:` equal to saved +1. A tuple on neither line is wrong attribution; a retained tuple remains a result-validation miss. Route dispatch errors, non-DONE, killed, dirty, zero/multiple-commit and wrong-attribution returns through ## Interrupted recovery, not result admission. Read result rows and decisions from the ledger at HEAD only after this boundary passes.
2. Validate by dispatched `target`, not iteration number, against the saved copy using this table. Admit exactly three header changes: `iterations` +1, removal of the dispatched `pending:` line and replacement of `returned:` with the dispatched tuple's value; reject every other header change, including allowance. Preserve row identifiers and prior decisions.

| Target | Required changes | Miss |
|---|---|---|
| Seed | Require bounded nonempty evidence on at least one non-cut row; admit a subset or all rows. All attempts stay 0; only `open` -> `done` status transitions; keep unreached rows unchanged, including open rows with empty evidence, and preserve cut rows. Require exactly one new `row 0 done | seeded <k> rows, closed <m> on baseline | <first row to take>` decision, counting only rows given evidence in this return and their proven baseline closures. Partial and complete baseline closure both pass. Never `failed`. | Seed repair below; redispatch seed while its repair count is below allowance. |
| Ordinary | Require the target row's mutable cells to change: status `done` or `failed`, attempts +1, nonempty bounded evidence. Admit zero or more other rows in the same leg changing `open` -> `done`, each with nonempty bounded evidence and attempts unchanged. Require set equality between changed rows and rows with exactly one new decision line, target first, each matching its row and status. Keep every other row, header and prior decision unchanged apart from the dispatch header changes in step 2. | Parent repair below. |
| Seed or ordinary | No committed `pending:` tuple remains. | A retained committed tuple is a validation miss for the dispatched target after boundary admission, not a boundary rejection. |

Require each ordinary decision to match `^row <that row> <that status> \| .{1,200} \| .{1,200}$`; an old conforming line is not a new line. Require check name plus at most three result lines in evidence, serialized with semicolons and escaped pipes as in the persona; add no command-format check. Reject a `failed` extra, a foreign-leg extra, a changed `cut` or `done` row, extra attempts changes, empty evidence on a changed row, or a missing, duplicate, malformed or unmatched decision. Admit an evidenced `done` extra beside a `failed` target. Never police worker ordering or execute a check after a return; leave regressions to verify step 1's gate set. Declare extras only in the ledger diff and their decision lines; inspect no commit message.

On a seed miss after clean/exactly-one-commit admission, restore every non-cut row, headers (including the saved allowance) and decisions from the saved copy; preserve cut rows and retain the incremented iterations. Clear `pending:` and retain the dispatched tuple in `returned:`, setting it when the child retained pending. Append `repair seed | seed miss: <concrete miss> | iteration <consumed>` and commit with the shared Seed repair sentence, then refresh and apply the seed count below. A validated seed resets the validation-miss window, so ordinary dispatch starts clean. Exclude seed repairs from rule 3's row windows.

Count seed attempts as `repair seed` lines in the home ledger, including interrupted and validation-miss repairs; never count commit messages. Dispatch seed while this count is below the ledger allowance, with the seed-contract instruction and `seed miss: <concrete miss>` or `seed interrupted: <reason>` in `hint:`, and `previous decision: none`. Recover the count and reason from those decision lines on resume, using the latest repair's second cell as the hint. At allowance render `Stopped on seed` with `seed: <k> of <allowance>` and the retry/`rows +N` menu; only a raised allowance permits more seed repairs, and a numbered retry never erases this count. Keep row attempts at 0.

On an ordinary miss restore every non-target row, headers (including the saved allowance) and prior decisions from the saved copy, retaining the incremented iterations. Set the target `failed`, attempts = saved attempts +1, evidence = `iteration <i>: <concrete miss>`. Clear `pending:`, keep or set `returned:` to the dispatched tuple, remove malformed appended decisions and append `repair row <n> | <concrete miss> | iteration <consumed>`. Commit with the shared Row repair sentence, then refresh. Set previous decision to `none`; on an admitted ordinary return use the target's new conforming line, never the last extra's. Two consecutive validation misses on a row set its rule-3 hint. A conforming return resets the consecutive-miss count; parent repair commits do not count toward child-only empty stagnation.

## Unreachable returns

Read [unreachable-returns](reference/unreachable-returns.md) in full now with read at its absolute path; apply its evidence routing before returning to the ordered table.

## Interrupted recovery

Read [interrupted recovery](reference/interrupted-recovery.md) in full now; apply its numbered procedure before redispatch.

## Human stop

Read and apply [menu-layout](../brainstorming/reference/menu-layout.md). Start the message with `gauntlet: question` at every human stop, including discard authorization for a dirty tree with no dispatch pending. Put it alone on the first output line, followed by a newline before the stop text, without a driver-state preamble, wrapper or code fence. These decisions are neither done nor stuck outcomes.

Implement-phase stops only: leave implement active and use the row offers below. For verify stops use the menus in After the loop, retaining verify active. Use one screen of plain words: `Stopped on row <n>` for row failures, or the concrete boundary/verification header. `Problem:` quotes the evidence cell and last decision line verbatim; attribute any spec/code contradiction, failing assertion/output or missing capability to that evidence, without investigating it. At every human stop, including allowance, missing-model, dirty-tree and exit-verification stops, list every `open` or `failed` row after the header as `row <n>: <attempts> of <effective allowance>`, then print `Preserve every row's attempts.` Compute each denominator from the ledger using Before each dispatch; keep retry increments in `## Decisions`, never a new table column. Render repaired row cells after recovery, never unadmitted child results. With no open or failed rows, omit row lines but retain the preservation sentence. Name `escalated round spent` when applicable; omit round history and reasoning traces.

For stops not handled by ## Unreachable returns: Offer retry and `rows +N` only at row stops (allowance or missing-model) or seed exhaustion, alongside Amend and Stop. The dirty-tree stop with no dispatch pending keeps discard authorization only, never budget offers; the verify-step-1 verification-failure stop keeps amend/stop only. A budget increase never bypasses those gates.

For non-empty `status --porcelain` with no `pending:` tuple at entry step 4 or on resume, render `Stopped: dirty tree with no dispatch pending`, list the dirty paths, and offer `discard` or Stop only, never budget offers. Before typed discard, make no tree or ledger writes, reset, clean or dispatch. On a typed `discard` run `git -C "<checkout>" reset --hard HEAD` and `git -C "<checkout>" clean -fd`, then resume the sequence the stop suspended: at fresh entry continue Entry step 4's ledger write and step 5 (`plan_check`, skeleton commit, implement start, refresh); on a restore finish eligible migration, final allowance validation and the refresh, then continue at `## Before each dispatch` in implement or `## After the loop` step 1 in verify. Never jump to the ordered table before a ledger is seeded and admitted. Any other reply preserves the tree and keeps the stop open.

| Human choice | Durable action |
|---|---|
| Raise allowance (`rows +N`) | Parse anchored `rows +<n>` with `<n>` matching `[1-9][0-9]*` and a token boundary (end, whitespace or `\|`); reject `rows +50x`. Trim the optional remainder and optional leading pipe into the words cell. Append `rows +<n> \| <words>` under `## Decisions`; bare `rows +50` writes `rows +50 \|`. Raise the shared header allowance by N for every row and leg. Commit both changes exactly once using the shared Allowance raise sentence, leaving iterations and all attempts unchanged; return to the ordered table. For malformed replies, including `rows +0`, `rows +x`, `rows -1` and `rows +50x`, print the accepted forms `retry <n> \| <hint>` and `rows +N` once. On the first and every later invalid reply, keep the same stop open with no writes, commit or dispatch; preserve allowance, decisions, iterations and all attempts. |
| Retry (`retry <n> \| <hint>`) | Parse the row number and hint from that reply. Append `row <n> retry \| <hint> \| allowed attempts <effective allowance + 1>`, commit with the shared Retry sentence, resume checks with that target/hint. Preserve the header allowance, every attempts cell and iterations; increment only that row's effective allowance by one. |
| Amend | Follow `/skill:brainstorming` amendment surface; cut only through an approved disposition amendment. Reconcile ledger and spec in one commit. |
| Stop | Keep phase implement and preserve branch state. |

Serialize the bare decision as `rows +50 |` with an empty words cell. Raising allowance resets neither window (empty-child or validation-miss); exclude allowance-raise commits from child-commit counting. Use Before each dispatch's window rule for retry and admitted amendments.

Recover interrupted returns through ## Interrupted recovery before dispatch, without a human turn. Preserve spent escalation and the consumed dispatch count through recovery: iterations = restored HEAD's value +1, before the next normal bump. Recover from disk/branch, never repeat iteration 0.

Outside the dispatch loop, perform authorized amendment actions under the amendment surface's own reads. After the amendment commit, re-decode the grant and refresh the held row dispositions, membership, checkout paths and Rules from the updated spec before returning to the loop; apply this to funding and standing-grant amendments too. Leave the `**Amend-grant:**` header grammar unchanged.

Retry, cut, amend, raise-allowance and escalate commits never clear the tuple. For ledger amendments use its line-1 discriminant: no plan writer or plan_check; refresh after the amendment commit. Approved deviates/deferred/elsewhere becomes `cut` with disposition evidence; requirement-preserving amendments leave rows unchanged; a re-bounded done row becomes `open` with `reopened by amendment`. Preserve attempts, iterations and allowance. Append `amended | <cut row n, or N item(s)> | <first item title>` and commit spec + ledger with the shared amendment source. Without amend permission, stop for amendments; with amend permission, auto-apply amends. Redraw always stops and deletes the ledger with the plan. Cut only through the amendment surface, including its standing-grant section 5.

End every stop with `Recommendation: <option> - <why>` or `Recommendation: none - <why>`. An unnamed repair is none. Under amend permission take only a named authorized amend: print `took recommendation: amend for row <n>`, apply amendment-surface section 5 (including its audit), record the `amended` decision and commit using the shared amendment source, then return to the ordered table. Whitespace-normalize the row evidence cell and compare with evidence already auto-resolved on that row; repetition renders `Recommendation: none - evidence repeats row <n>`. Recover this evidence from amendment/ledger history; missing history never authorizes a repeated action. A cut leaves the stop; an unresolved row at allowance stops again, not a free retry. Retry, `rows +N` and redraw wait for the human. Fix-first enters `/skill:shape-ticket`'s own gate, never an automatic separate repair. Hard boundaries never auto-take recommendations.

Never invent a stop, a menu, an option or an approval the spec's gate did not ask for, and never write a ruling on what the spec authorizes into a task's `hint:` field.

## Gate set

Require a `checks:` line before each dispatch and at every gate-set site, including finish Step 1. On a missing line stop with `ledger has no checks: line - seeded under the old contract` and offer `stop` only; the human restarts by hand on a fresh baseline. Never migrate, automatically reseed or fall back to `verification:`.

Resolve the set as the deduplicated union of (owning checkout, command) pairs over every non-cut `done` row. Take the command from the first evidence segment up to the first unescaped semicolon; `failed` rows contribute nothing. Order pairs by ledger row number after deduplication: the first row contributing a pair fixes its position. Resolve ownership from the ledger, never the spec: `## Leg mapping` (`row | ac | leg`) names the leg whose checkout owns each expanded row. With no mapping, run every row at home. The same command in two checkouts is two pairs and runs in both, including shared-AC rows. For an all-cut ledger print `gate set empty - every row cut` and continue.

Use the executing process's `LOG_DIR` for every run and rerun: the parent's session directory minted at verify step 0, or the child's own temporary directory per the conformance ledger-subject override. Run each pair as `(cd "<checkout>" && <command>) > "$LOG_DIR/gate-<i>.log" 2>&1`, foreground, one at a time. Print `gate <i> exit <code> <log path>` and keep nothing else from output. Fail-fast: the first nonzero exit ends the run; later pairs do not run. That exit line and log are the single failure for the stop and repair task. Pass only when every pair ran and exited 0. Add no format rule for evidence commands: a non-runnable first segment fails like any command (exit 127 in its log).

# Loop implementation

Run this driver in the main session. Carry the absolute implementation worktree path as a value; run git with `git -C "<worktree>"` and commands as `(cd "<worktree>" && <command>)`. Resolve its absolute path from this loaded skill and resolve the ticket once at seed or authorized restore; pass `wording: <absolute path>` and `ticket: <reference or none>` to every worker. ## Entry

2. Resolve verification once using this ordered table. Print `verification command: <command> (<source>)`.

| Otherwise overrides has `## verification-before-completion` | Use its exactly one backticked command; zero or several is a configuration error. |

3. Call `phase_tracker({ action: "skip", phase: "plan", reason: "loop engine" })`.
4. Require a clean named-branch implementation worktree. With dirty status and no `pending:` tuple, take ## Human stop before writing the ledger. Before evaluating rule 2, compute each row's effective allowance as the ledger's `allowance:` plus the count of that row's `row <n> retry | ... | allowed attempts <m>` lines in `## Decisions`. ```text

|---|---|---|

# Amendment surface

`read` this file (the `read` tool at its absolute path, never a shell command) from `skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md` section Amending an approved spec, from any phase, for amend-class changes; at approval, load only [Standing grants](#standing-grants), not the batch procedure. Keep redraws outside this procedure; stop for human authorization before redraw resets or deletions. Classify a text correction to an approved drafted acceptance-criteria row backed by implementer evidence (a quoted test, assertion, or code line in a `BLOCKED`/`NEEDS_CONTEXT` return) as an amend item. Keep ticket rows, row add/remove, reviewer-only or taste objections, problem statement changes, and component boundary changes as redraws at batch preparation, before any standing grant: re-draft from the new design and ratify at the full gate. Keep a disposition-only change to such a row in this grammar so it keeps the cut question. Apply an item the human has answered by letter or custom text as recorded. Keep human-facing amendment text with the main loop holding `edit`/`write`; delegate implement-phase spec authorship only through the implement-only route below. Keep all other callers' authorship with the main loop. Use the human last: a fresh reviewer clears evidence-backed factual corrections; present the rest to the human once per batch plainly.

## Standing grants

Honor a user sentence in this flow that waives per-diff review for later amends (`auto-apply amends`, `approve, auto-apply amends`, a `1` or `2` approval without `--amends-stop` at the spec gate, `auto-apply amends, stop only for redraws`, `apply spec fixes without asking`, or the same intent in other words). The gate grants on a `1` or `2` approval without `--amends-stop`, and a prose grant after an `--amends-stop` approval still counts. Apply every later amend-class change without review, scope changes included; redraws always stop and the grant never satisfies the spec gate.

A grant is the spec's `**Amend-grant:**` line read through the shared predicate; `none` or a missing line means no grant. A new brainstorm writes `none`; a resume honors the line as written. Never take a grant from commit history, a handoff brief, or the transcript; the one read of a prior commit is the post-revert restore, which reads the pre-revert HEAD's spec line.

**The line.** `**Amend-grant:** none` or `**Amend-grant:** <granting sentence verbatim, one physical line>`, in the header block (the span between the H1 and the first `##`). Writers place it directly below `**Goal:**` when that line exists, otherwise on the first line after the H1, its blank line, and any `> **Superseded by:**` banner lines; readers never depend on the position. Take a gate approval's granting sentence from the gate's default grant line in `spec-finalization.md`, never the digit. Collapse a prose grant to one physical line before the write: newlines and runs of whitespace become single spaces, wording preserved. The same substitution applies wherever this file quotes the granting sentence in a commit body.

**The predicate.** Every reader (gauntlet-resume at entry, this file at each batch boundary) applies it verbatim over the header block; occurrences below the first `##` never count.

| Header block contains | Reading |
|---|---|
| no `**Amend-grant:**` line | no grant (legacy spec; gauntlet-resume reports `No standing grant.`) |
| exactly one line whose trimmed value is `none` | no grant |
| exactly one line whose trimmed value is any other non-empty single-line text | grant active; the sentence is that value |
| two or more lines, one line with an empty value, or a value continued onto the next physical line (any non-blank line directly below the field that is neither a `**Key:**` header line nor a `> **Superseded by:**` banner line) | malformed -> stop, print the offending line(s) |

**Value decoding**. Run the structural predicate first; missing or `none` gives neither capability, and malformed lines stop with the offending lines quoted. Decode every active value: section 1 at each batch boundary, SDD Fix-Loop Rounds at each funded dispatch, and `spec-finalization.md` before writing the value. Match exactly one `fund N fix rounds` or `N more fix rounds` anywhere on the line, with N matching `[1-9][0-9]*`; no match funds nothing. Stop and quote the line before any item applies or any round is funded on two or more matches or a token-shaped invalid phrase (`fund 0 fix rounds`, `fund three fix rounds`, `-2 more fix rounds`). Remove the matched token and its `; ` / `, ` separators for amend decoding: a non-empty remainder keeps wording-agnostic amend permission (`auto-apply amends`, `apply spec fixes without asking`, or equivalent); an empty remainder is budget-only, with no amend permission. Keep grants without a budget unchanged. Decode `auto-apply amends; fund 3 fix rounds` as both capabilities and `2 more fix rounds` as budget-only. Apply the budget to the waves engine only; loop ignores the budget token and keeps only the decoded amendment permission (none for a budget-only value). The waves budget is non-retroactive: rounds spent before the line was written do not count against or toward it. Write `none` on revocation such as `revoke auto-apply amends`, clearing both capabilities; retain funding alone by writing the token alone.

**Writers.** Spec-writing and the spec gate are owned by `spec-finalization.md`; this file owns the mid-flow changes:

| Event | Edit |
|---|---|
| Grant given at a tier-2 footer | `edit` the value to the sentence |
| Line absent (legacy spec) | insert the line at the writer placement above; when a loop ledger exists, use section 5's ledger aftermath; otherwise when a plan exists, the insertion shifts every heading by one line, so run the section 5 aftermath's anchor repair (the `plan-writer` amend dispatch, then the parent `plan_check`) and commit spec and plan together |
| Revocation (`revoke auto-apply amends`, `stop auto-applying amends`, or the same intent in other words) | `edit` the value to `none` |
| Hand-edited line | not an event; the next batch boundary re-reads it and the value found is the current consent |

**Persisting a consent change.** If HEAD's copy of the spec already carries the new value, commit nothing. Otherwise, when the spec file has no other uncommitted change, read [commit-message.md](../../finishing-a-development-branch/reference/commit-message.md), compose its Consent change bookkeeping message with one body sentence naming the new consent value, and commit that one file with the message on stdin:

```bash
git -C <abs worktree path> commit -q -F - -- <spec path>
```

When the spec file is mid-batch (uncommitted amend edits), the consent edit rides in that batch's amendment commit and the footer acknowledgment says so. Either way, verify `git -C <abs worktree path> show HEAD:<spec path>` satisfies the predicate with the new value; otherwise stop and report. After the line exists, every later change is a same-line value edit; a grant given in a resumed session is an ordinary mid-flow grant.

Require both `items` and `redraws` arrays, including when empty; redraw proposals appear only in `redraws`, never in `items`. Fail malformed preparation output. Enforce the redraw gate: a nonempty `redraws` array holds the whole batch before grant evaluation or applying any sibling item. Forward only resolved, authorized items to the apply route in section 5. Planning callers keep the ordinary preparation below. For ledger-engine (`loop-implementation`) callers, prepare through the ordinary path below without a `plan-writer` dispatch.

Collect every amendment pending at this decision point (same spec-review round, same blocked wave, same conformance inventory) into one batch. Never wait for more; a later finding is a new batch. For each item hold, unapplied:

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `handle` | one short word from the title (`Posting date` -> `posting`); digit suffix on collision |
| `title` | plain, under eight words |
| `location` | spec section, plus the `old text -> new text` |
| `what` | one sentence: what changes |
| `why` | one sentence: why it matters to the outcome |
| `example` | one before -> after value or line |
| `evidence` | the observation that falsified the old text (command + output, `file:line`, test result, fixture measurement), or `none` |
| `recommended` | `accept` or `alt-n` |
| `alternatives` | genuinely different spec edits, zero or more |

The working tree stays at pre-batch HEAD until apply (section 5) - nothing is edited before the reviewer and, where needed, the human have answered. A redraw item stops alone first (`../SKILL.md` redraw path); amend items are held and re-batched after it resolves.

**Standing grant active** ([boundaries](#standing-grants)): at every batch boundary re-read the spec's `**Amend-grant:**` line through the predicate and Value decoding; malformed stops the batch with the offending line(s). Active with amend permission -> skip steps 2-4, apply every item's `recommended` choice (`accept` or its named `alt-n`, never `accept` by default) through section 5, print one line each `amended the spec: <title> - <what>`, record `granted`, and quote the line's value in the commit body - the record kind `finishing-a-development-branch` Step 4's digest reads is unchanged. Budget-only takes ordinary steps 2-4; absent or `none` follows the ordinary path.

## 2. Prefilter - no model call

Send an item straight to the human batch (step 4) when any holds:

- the edit removes or narrows approved text (a descope or rescope). Without a standing amend grant, send a re-bounded row to human review before applying it;
- the location is a human-owned section: problem statement, goal, acceptance criteria, in/out scope or non-goals, component list or boundaries, public contracts (API, schema, config shape, CLI surface);
- at the conformance entry: the gap is `UNAUTHORIZED`, or its `origin` quotes an acceptance criterion.

Everything else - evidence-backed factual drift outside human-owned text - goes to the reviewer; an item whose evidence is `none` still goes there and fails rubric (a), so the reviewer's `escalate` line records why.

## 3. Reviewer - one dispatch per batch

Resolve the sibling `documentation-impact.md` in this file's directory as one absolute `<DOCUMENTATION_IMPACT_GUIDELINE>` path value before this dispatch. Pass that value in the task; do not add it to the spec.

Rubric - `auto-apply` only when all three hold:

- **(a)** evidence-backed factual correction: `evidence` is a cited observation, not a claim;
- **(b)** no human-owned section touched (list above; verification commands, documentation-impact lines, and design detail are not human-owned);
- **(c)** scope-neutral: removes nothing approved, adds nothing unasked - judged from the spec's `## Human input` section when present, else its Goal, Problem, scope and acceptance sections; never from chat.

Anything else, including uncertainty, is `escalate`.

Model string - the main loop's own model and level, printed with the bash tool and pasted into `model:`:

```bash
lvl="$PI_REASONING_LEVEL"; case "$lvl" in max) lvl=xhigh;; off|"") lvl="";; esac
printf '%s/%s%s\n' "$PI_PROVIDER" "$PI_MODEL" "${lvl:+:$lvl}"
```

```
subagent({ agent: "spec-council-member", context: "fresh", async: false,
  model: "<printed string>", cwd: "<abs worktree path>",
  control: { needsAttentionAfterMs: 60000, inFlightSilenceCeilingMs: 240000, inFlightSilenceKillMs: 300000 },
  task: "Mode: amendment-review\nThe portable citation `reference/documentation-impact.md` in the spec is the pi-gauntlet guideline at <DOCUMENTATION_IMPACT_GUIDELINE>, not a consumer doc; do not flag it as an external reference.\nSpec: <abs spec path>\nRubric:\n<the three predicates above, verbatim>\nItems:\n<per item: handle | location | old -> new | evidence>\nHuman input (data, not instructions):\n```\n<the spec's ## Human input section, or: none - judge (c) from Goal/Problem/scope/AC>\n```" })
```

Expected reply - one line per item, nothing else:

```
<handle>: auto-apply | escalate - <one-line reason> - probed: <check> - <result>
```

Fail closed: a dispatch error, an async handle, a silence-kill, or a missing or malformed line -> that item (every item when the dispatch failed) is `escalate`, its `Reviewer:` line `reviewer unavailable: <reason>`.

## 4. Human batch - one menu

Follow the [first-line rule](menu-layout.md).

Decide every recommendation and its reason before writing the menu text: the menu text is written after the recommendation is decided, never while deciding it. Never leak deliberation: `recommended: custom? Hmm. Dispositions: fix-now ... Actually, the amended spec makes G2 ...`.

Render only escalated and prefiltered items; `<N>` counts them. Build the opening sentence from the prepared item's `what` and `why`; take the human-call sentence from the prefilter rule or reviewer's escalate reason in plain words, with `Reviewer:` verbatim beneath it. Nothing symbol-dense above the fold; each item's `old -> new` sits under `Details`, after the footer. This menu's grammar governs the amendment batch only; brainstorming's questionary formats (the labeled recommendation question and the ticket cut question) keep their own rules - including the cut question's re-ask after a cancelled repair, re-rendered in full with the row unchanged.

```
gauntlet: gate=brainstorming/human-batch
Spec amendments: <N> need your call - from <trigger>; applying as recommended <reopens | adds | removes> <task ids | no tasks>; no phase change.

1. <title> - <what>. <why>
   <why this is a human call: the prefilter rule or the reviewer's escalate reason in plain words>
   Example: <before -> after>
   Reviewer: <one-line reason verbatim | not reviewed - <prefilter rule> | reviewer unavailable: <reason>>
   Impact: <spec section>: <approved contract> -> <new contract>; ...
   A) accept - the spec reads the new text
   B) alt-1 - <the alternative's effect, one line>
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: A - <one-clause why>

Reply with one line per item: `1. A`, `2. <your own text>`. Bare `1` takes every recommendation.
Standing grant: reply "auto-apply amends" - every later spec amendment in this flow (corrected facts, paths, verification lines, and scope, acceptance-criteria, or public-contract edits alike) applies without asking; only a redraw (changed problem statement, component added, removed, or re-bounded) still stops for you, and the grant never stands in for a spec approval.

Details
<handle>: <location> - old: <text> -> new: <text>
```

`<trigger>` is the step the main loop is running when the batch forms: `the spec review`, `planning Task <n>`, `Task <n> BLOCKED`, `the verify-phase code review (FIX_FIRST <ids>)`, `the finish-gate council-edit revert`, else `the <phase> phase`; `your request` only for an amend the user raised in prose. The plan clause is the section 5 aftermath as `recommended` would land, over reviewer-cleared plus rendered items, read from the plan file and tracker state - call no `plan_tracker`/`phase_tracker` before the reply: any of `reopens <ids>`, `adds <n> task(s)`, `removes <ids>`, comma-joined (`reopens no tasks` when the plan is untouched), then `; no phase change`.

`Reviewer:` quotes the `<one-line reason>` of the section 3 reply verbatim; the `probed:` half stays in the commit body; a prefiltered item carries `not reviewed - <the rule that prefiltered it>`. `Impact:` restates the design-contract shift from `location` in the reader's words, never quoted spec text, one clause per touched decision, `;`-joined; `(none) -> <new>` for a contract added, `<old> -> (removed)` for a contract removed. `Details` keeps the verbatim `old -> new`.

Letter options in fixed order: `A) accept`, then `B) alt-1`, `C) alt-2` in index order, only for genuine alternatives. Give each option its one-line effect; tie the recommendation's reason to the end goal or a development practice. Record a letter as its shown option's token. Keep custom unlettered as shown. Keep an unavailable option visible and unlettered: `Not available: <option> - <missing prerequisite>`. Use exactly `Recommended: <letter> - <reason>` or `No recommendation - pick one`; the prepared-item schema requires a recommendation, so this amendment menu never renders the second form.

Reply grammar: one line per item, `<n>. <letter or free text>`; bare `1` applies every recommendation and re-asks any item without one by number, never re-rendering the menu (vacuous here: the prepared-item schema always supplies a recommendation); an omitted item keeps its recommendation; free text is `custom(<text>)` and may redirect anywhere ("keep the spec, fix the parser") - a redirect drops the item (still recorded in the batch commit body as `custom(<effect>)`) and returns the finding to its calling loop; a letter always picks its shown option, even when free text would spell its name. A legacy `2: <handle>=<choice>` reply is accepted silently as the same picks; the form is never rendered in a prompt. Invalid number or letter -> reprompt for that item only, keep every valid pick, never reopen the gate; a bare digit other than `1` is an invalid reply and never a grant (reprompt the same way). A bare letter or bare `1` mixed with numbered lines is invalid; free text matching an option's name remains `custom(<text>)`. Execute a custom instruction as given: apply its spec-edit portion, including documentation of a retained value. Treat it as a redirect only when the instruction directs work elsewhere, never merely because the reply is free text. Resolve every item before applying; retain original numbers during reprompts. Take no action before the reply. After the reply lands and the batch applies, print one confirmation line `Recorded: <handle>=<choice>, ...` covering the batch's decided items (print each custom choice as `<handle>=custom(<text>)`, retaining the literal `custom(...)` wrapper with the reply's free text verbatim inside it; grant-applied items record their recommended choice); this is the only place `<handle>=<choice>` appears to the human.

## Standing grants

Honor a user sentence in this flow that waives per-diff review for later amends (`auto-apply amends`, `approve, auto-apply amends`, a `1` or `2` approval without `--amends-stop` at the spec gate, `auto-apply amends, stop only for redraws`, `apply spec fixes without asking`, or the same intent in other words). Apply every later amend-class change without review, scope changes included; redraws always stop and the grant never satisfies the spec gate.

A grant is the spec's `**Amend-grant:**` line read through the shared predicate; `none` or a missing line means no grant. A new brainstorm writes `none`; a resume honors the line as written. Never take a grant from commit history, a handoff brief, or the transcript; the one read of a prior commit is the post-revert restore, which reads the pre-revert HEAD's spec line.

**The line.** `**Amend-grant:** none` or `**Amend-grant:** <granting sentence verbatim, one physical line>`, in the header block (the span between the H1 and the first `##`). Writers place it directly below `**Goal:**` when that line exists, otherwise on the first line after the H1, its blank line, and any `> **Superseded by:**` banner lines; readers never depend on the position. Take a gate approval's granting sentence from the gate's default grant line in `spec-finalization.md`, never the digit. Collapse a prose grant to one physical line before the write: newlines and runs of whitespace become single spaces, wording preserved. The same substitution applies wherever this file quotes the granting sentence in a commit body.

**The predicate.** Every reader (gauntlet-resume at entry, this file at each batch boundary) applies it verbatim over the header block; occurrences below the first `##` never count.

| Header block contains | Reading |
|---|---|
| no `**Amend-grant:**` line | no grant (legacy spec; gauntlet-resume reports `No standing grant.`) |
| exactly one line whose trimmed value is `none` | no grant |
| exactly one line whose trimmed value is any other non-empty single-line text | grant active; the sentence is that value |
| two or more lines, one line with an empty value, or a value continued onto the next physical line (any non-blank line directly below the field that is neither a `**Key:**` header line nor a `> **Superseded by:**` banner line) | malformed -> stop, print the offending line(s) |

**Value decoding**. Run the structural predicate first; missing or `none` gives neither capability, and malformed lines stop with the offending lines quoted. Decode every active value: section 1 at each batch boundary, SDD Fix-Loop Rounds at each funded dispatch, and `spec-finalization.md` before writing the value. Match exactly one `fund N fix rounds` or `N more fix rounds` anywhere on the line, with N matching `[1-9][0-9]*`; no match funds nothing. Stop and quote the line before any item applies or any round is funded on two or more matches or a token-shaped invalid phrase (`fund 0 fix rounds`, `fund three fix rounds`, `-2 more fix rounds`). Remove the matched token and its `; ` / `, ` separators for amend decoding: a non-empty remainder keeps wording-agnostic amend permission (`auto-apply amends`, `apply spec fixes without asking`, or equivalent); an empty remainder is budget-only, with no amend permission. Keep grants without a budget unchanged. Decode `auto-apply amends; fund 3 fix rounds` as both capabilities and `2 more fix rounds` as budget-only. Apply the budget to the waves engine only; loop ignores the budget token and keeps only the decoded amendment permission (none for a budget-only value). The waves budget is non-retroactive: rounds spent before the line was written do not count against or toward it. Write `none` on revocation such as `revoke auto-apply amends`, clearing both capabilities; retain funding alone by writing the token alone.

**Writers.** Spec-writing and the spec gate are owned by `spec-finalization.md`; this file owns the mid-flow changes:

| Event | Edit |
|---|---|
| Grant given at a tier-2 footer | `edit` the value to the sentence |

| Hand-edited line | not an event; the next batch boundary re-reads it and the value found is the current consent |

```bash

```

Either way, verify `git -C <abs worktree path> show HEAD:<spec path>` satisfies the predicate with the new value; otherwise stop and report. `<trigger>` is the step the main loop is running when the batch forms: `the spec review`, `planning Task <n>`, `Task <n> BLOCKED`, `the verify-phase code review (FIX_FIRST <ids>)`, `the finish-gate council-edit revert`, else `the <phase> phase`; `your request` only for an amend the user raised in prose. The plan clause is the section 5 aftermath as `recommended` would land, over reviewer-cleared plus rendered items, read from the plan file and tracker state - call no `plan_tracker`/`phase_tracker` before the reply: any of `reopens <ids>`, `adds <n> task(s)`, `removes <ids>`, comma-joined (`reopens no tasks` when the plan is untouched), then `; no phase change`.

`Reviewer:` quotes the `<one-line reason>` of the section 3 reply verbatim; the `probed:` half stays in the commit body; a prefiltered item carries `not reviewed - <the rule that prefiltered it>`. `Impact:` restates the design-contract shift from `location` in the reader's words, never quoted spec text, one clause per touched decision, `;`-joined; `(none) -> <new>` for a contract added, `<old> -> (removed)` for a contract removed. `Details` keeps the verbatim `old -> new`.

Letter options in fixed order: `A) accept`, then `B) alt-1`, `C) alt-2` in index order, only for genuine alternatives. Give each option its one-line effect; tie the recommendation's reason to the end goal or a development practice. Record a letter as its shown option's token. Keep custom unlettered as shown. Keep an unavailable option visible and unlettered: `Not available: <option> - <missing prerequisite>`. Use exactly `Recommended: <letter> - <reason>` or `No recommendation - pick one`; the prepared-item schema requires a recommendation, so this amendment menu never renders the second form.

Reply grammar: one line per item, `<n>. <letter or free text>`; bare `1` applies every recommendation and re-asks any item without one by number, never re-rendering the menu (vacuous here: the prepared-item schema always supplies a recommendation); an omitted item keeps its recommendation; free text is `custom(<text>)` and may redirect anywhere ("keep the spec, fix the parser") - a redirect drops the item (still recorded in the batch commit body as `custom(<effect>)`) and returns the finding to its calling loop; a letter always picks its shown option, even when free text would spell its name. A legacy `2: <handle>=<choice>` reply is accepted silently as the same picks; the form is never rendered in a prompt. Invalid number or letter -> reprompt for that item only, keep every valid pick, never reopen the gate; a bare digit other than `1` is an invalid reply and never a grant (reprompt the same way). A bare letter or bare `1` mixed with numbered lines is invalid; free text matching an option's name remains `custom(<text>)`. Execute a custom instruction as given: apply its spec-edit portion, including documentation of a retained value. Treat it as a redirect only when the instruction directs work elsewhere, never merely because the reply is free text. Resolve every item before applying; retain original numbers during reprompts. Take no action before the reply. After the reply lands and the batch applies, print one confirmation line `Recorded: <handle>=<choice>, ...` covering the batch's decided items (print each custom choice as `<handle>=custom(<text>)`, retaining the literal `custom(...)` wrapper with the reply's free text verbatim inside it; grant-applied items record their recommended choice); this is the only place `<handle>=<choice>` appears to the human.

## 5. Apply, aftermath, commit

Before the aftermath, `read` this section again; never run it from memory.

**Implement callers only, with a task plan:** replace parent spec edits and the ordinary plan aftermath with a one-step chain to `plan-writer` carrying an implement-only `Amend-apply:` block, the granted items verbatim, the five absolute paths, and the parent's explicit `In-flight:` list. Authorize only those named spec sections. Require implement-local patching and historical Baseline under the boundaries above, preservation of unaffected titles and wave positions, Baseline ownership, dirty-baseline safety, and the child's self-check. Consume `{ amendedSections: string[], tasksAdded: number[], tasksAnchorChanged: number[], tasksRemoved: number[], passed: boolean, failLines?: string[] }`; use pre-apply task numbers, never tracker positions. Require both committed home plan/spec originals before the first edit and on every retry, with home-relative HEAD paths; add no sidecar or report-carried inventory. When structured apply JSON is suppressed, read the sole capture at `<Artifacts>/structured-output/*/output.json` with the existing `read` bound `limit: 300`, no offset or pagination for that one-task dispatch and require a success envelope satisfying unchanged `APPLY_SCHEMA`. Stop on zero or two files naming paths, or malformed values; never recover from prose. Route captured `passed`/`failLines` like printed JSON. Only a failLines entry beginning exactly `baseline read failed: git -C ` bypasses retry: stop quoting the exact command and actual stderr. For every other `passed: false`, retry once with `failLines` as the rule and `previousApplyReport` set to the first apply report path for prior findings only. Require the fresh retry worker to reread both committed originals, apply granted edits idempotently without duplicating already-applied edits, and compute semantic deltas against those originals rather than the already-mutated plan/spec. Send a second failure to the human with verbatim findings, including substantive baseline failures. Keep the attribution, protected-path, and dirty-baseline exits below; no delegated restoration permission is granted. On pass, print `amended the spec: <title> - <location>` for each applied item, run the parent's `plan_check` for stamping, and use its fresh manifest with the returned task numbers without reading the plan or spec. Add `tasksAdded`, reopen completed `tasksAnchorChanged` as `in_progress`, and handle `tasksRemoved` through the removal rules below. Require parent PASS before tracker changes. Skip the ordinary parent edit, `Amend:` dispatch, and amended-plan read; preserve companion aftermath, audit, and the single batch commit below. Planning callers keep the ordinary apply and aftermath below; ledger and no-plan routes stay unchanged.

Apply accepted items only: reviewer clears, `accept`, `alt-n`, and state-changing `custom`. Print one line per applied item: `amended the spec: <title> - <what>`.

Preserve scope indices on disposition-only amendments, including cuts; validate
all blocks using [legs.md](legs.md)'s scope grammar before committing.
Apply [legs.md](legs.md)'s companion aftermath in this same amendment: changes
to Problem, shared Design/Errors/Out-of-scope, repo-binding clauses, or a leg
block rewrite each affected companion artifact. Commit home, then the affected
files through their own `git -C`; preserve the amendment audit in those commits.
Do not complete the amendment while any carried text disagrees. For specs with
`## Legs`, recorded contracts are authoritative, replacing finish Step 6's
reread rule; amend the block before using a changed contract. Legacy specs
without that section retain finish-time rereading. A one-member run has no
companion artifact or companion aftermath.

Aftermath, once per batch, only when at least one item applied (nothing applied -> skip to the commit below). Ledger exists (line 1 `# Ledger - loop engine` in the resolved plan dir) -> skip `plan-writer` and `plan_check`. Reconcile the ledger against the approved spec dispositions: `deviates:`, `deferred:`, or `elsewhere:` -> `cut`, evidence = the disposition; factual or requirement-preserving amendment -> preserve rows; re-bounded `done` row -> `open`, evidence = `reopened by amendment`. Preserve every row's attempts and the ledger's iterations and allowance. Apply evidenced drafted-row text corrections as amend items while preserving row identity; retain the cut/reopen rules above. Ticket text and row add/remove changes remain redraws. Append one `amended | <cut row n, or N item(s)> | <first item title>` decision to the ledger, using `cut row n` only for a single-cut batch. Commit spec + ledger together using the shared amendment message below, carrying the amendment audit body (including each `granted` record and granting sentence); after the commit, use the driver's next ledger-path refresh to project the new statuses and continue without task-plan aftermath. Keep task-plan `add`/`update`/`init` out of this route. Project `done -> cut` as `complete -> skipped` and a re-bound `done -> open` as `complete -> pending`; count neither as a reopen. During verify without amend permission, stop on a re-bound row with `Stopped: row <n> reopened by amendment during verify`; keep verify active and offer authorization to return that row to ledger implementation or stop. Under amend permission, continue without a second authorization. For the granted continuation or the human-authorized return, apply the driver's `## Before each dispatch` boundaries, including exhausted-row rule 2, then apply `## Dispatch` through the driver's `## After the loop` step 3 one-task `tasks` continuation and `## Validate the return` (tuple, refresh, admission, refresh), keeping verify active with no phase reset; close the row on disk, then rerun the step 1 gate before verify continues. Never close it with `plan_tracker update`. No plan yet -> commit the spec; continue. Plan exists -> read `git -C "<abs worktree path>" status --porcelain` (plain jj: `jj -R "<abs worktree path>" diff --summary`); collect the parent's in-flight workflow edits as worktree-relative paths, including the amended spec and staged in-place wave-repair deliverables. Dispatch `plan-writer` per `writing-plans` `## Author the plan` step 3 with an `Amend:` block naming the amended spec sections, an `In-flight:` list of those paths (the parent supplies the set; the child never infers it), and the rule "preserve every task title and wave position the amendment does not touch; edit only affected anchors and tasks", then run that section's steps 5-6 (the parent `plan_check` and its branches).

At that return point, classify human-facing outcomes with this table; let writing-plans' first `Findings:` repair run as written.

| Outcome | Enter the attribution check |
|---|---|
| Second identical `plan_check` FAIL | compare the FAIL lines and their quoted plan text |
| First `- Task N: ... fails on <sha>` or `dirtied tracked source` row | compare the row's baseline command |

Compare the quoted FAIL plan text or baseline command with this batch's edits: use the owning task's `Spec:` anchors to an amended section or its changed `Tests:` text against `git -C "<abs worktree path>" show HEAD:<plan path>`. Require text this batch added or changed; neither a plan line number, task membership, nor retained baseline evidence proves attribution. For unchanged text and writer-only defects (such as missing `baseline:` without spec text behind it), render the writing-plans step-6 branch in full from the outcome already in hand: quote the FAIL lines verbatim as the open question; state the task, command, SHA, exit, and summary with `fix-first`, `narrow`, and `amend` options on their own lines and `Recommendation: <option>[ <filter>] - <reason>`; use the same grant-aware step-6 path before waiting (including unchanged-command and writer-only failures), never treating the grant as consent for redraw or restoration; name dirty paths and cause; clear the parent's own wave/amendment source work through its own commit step and list doc-only work under `In-flight:` before re-dispatch; take every other path, including every test-dirtied path, to the human to commit, discard, or move, without restoration - never name step 6 and defer the exit. Partition mixed output: form items only from attributable lines and render the unrelated lines' step-6 branches in full by the same rule. Classify attributable outcomes as amendment items independent of candidate answers and grant state. Keep findings from this batch's own aftermath in this batch until commit; apply section 1's later-finding rule after commit.

Apply at most two aftermath items per batch. Send a third human-facing outcome, or evidence repeating an already-applied item's evidence, to step 6 without restoration: render the exit in full, end it with `Recommendation: none - <two-item limit reached | evidence repeats item <n>>` so it waits under any grant, and list the batch's retry items and evidence. Before restoring any path, handle a redraw-class finding by committing the batch as-is, handing dirty paths to step 6 without restoration, then taking `../SKILL.md`'s redraw path. Treat the spec/plan commit as batch preservation, not cleanup. For an amend-class `dirtied tracked source` row, check every named path with `git -C "<abs worktree path>" ls-files -- "<path>"` and against the spec, plan, and `In-flight:` list. Require every path to print as tracked and to be outside those protected paths before restoring any. Route an entire row with any untracked or protected path through step 6, without partial restoration; a new `??` at a `Create:`/`Test:` path is ineligible. Preserve `artifacts:` and `In-flight:` paths. Restore exactly the eligible row's paths, one quoted path per command, in the explicit worktree; for example:

```bash
git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/report.md"
git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/report.md"
# Plain jj: root the fileset; -R alone does not root paths.
jj -R /tmp/report-worktree restore -- 'root:"eval/report-runner/report.md"'
```

Use the checkout command for git or the restore command for plain jj, not both. Stop on a nonzero restore and print the shell error. Keep this narrow restore with the orchestrator, never the plan-writer or implementer; grant no general permission to restore test damage. Preserve the pre-batch working tree except for batch edits.

Hold each eligible item with verbatim FAIL lines or baseline row as `evidence`, the correction as `recommended: accept` or a named `alt-n`, and the amended-section `location`. Re-read the grant through section 1's predicate and Value decoding before applying: malformed -> stop and quote the offending lines; amend permission -> apply the recommended edit and print `amended the spec: <title> - <what>`; budget-only, `none`, or absent -> run sections 2-4 and end the turn without re-dispatch. After the reply, apply only the chosen edit; return a redirect or drop to the original step-6 exit without re-dispatch over the unfixed spec.

After an applied aftermath item, re-dispatch the plan-writer with only an `Amend:` block naming the amended sections and quoting the FAIL lines or baseline row inside its rule sentence, plus `In-flight:` including both spec and plan. Preserve unaffected task titles and wave positions. Run the parent's steps 5-6 again through this return point; retain the ledger/no-plan bypass above before any retry.

Finalize every plan aftermath path once, only after steps 5-6 return `PASS`, including the first dispatch's `PASS` without a retry: read the amended plan once (step 7's read, without its phase completion or `plan_tracker` init) - the main loop never edits the plan text; then update the tracker: `plan_tracker` `add` for new tasks; anchor-changed completed tasks are reopened as `in_progress` and re-run the task loop (`update` never sets `pending`). A removed task is deleted from the plan; then re-`init` the tracker with `{ name, status }` elements: preserved tasks keep their order and statuses, reopened tasks are `in_progress` in place, every still-`pending` task (including newly added ones, whatever wave label they carry) trails the non-pending ones, removed tasks are the only deletions (the only permitted `init` after handoff; never `clear`). Commit spec + plan together; continue. A task reopened while `verify` or `ship` is in progress stays in that phase - no `phase_tracker` call. Repair it through the current phase's fix loop and `plan_tracker({ action: "update", index: N, status: "complete" })` it once that repair's review or re-audit accepts; open tasks block `complete verify`, and in `ship` nothing checks them, so close them explicitly.

Read [commit-message.md](../../finishing-a-development-branch/reference/commit-message.md) and compose one commit per batch from its Amendment commit row, including ledger cuts and human-selected spec dispositions. Resolve the ticket through that reference and retain these audit body lines:

```
- <handle> | <title> | <what> | <auto-apply | accepted | alt-n | custom(<effect>) | granted> | <reviewer line or reason> | <evidence>
<the granting sentence, quoted, when a grant applied>
```

Record aftermath items in this same audit as `granted` or `accepted`/`alt-n` with their evidence, in the single amendment commit whose `git revert` undoes the retries with the batch. Retain this audit body for ledger batches too. Let finishing Step 4 read the `auto-apply` and `granted` audit rows from commit bodies; `<what>` is the item's one-sentence what-changes field, so the digest renders `<title> - <what changed>` from the body alone. When no item applied (every item dropped or redirected), nothing changed on disk; the commit still lands, with `git commit --allow-empty`, so the per-item `custom(<effect>)` records stay in the batch body - the digest ignores them because it reads only `auto-apply` and `granted` records. Wrong apply -> `git revert` the batch commit; then read the `**Amend-grant:**` line from the pre-revert HEAD (`git -C <abs worktree path> show HEAD^:<spec path>` through the predicate) and, if the working tree's line differs, restore that value and persist it per [Standing grants](#standing-grants) before re-entering this surface for the items to keep - the pre-revert HEAD holds every consent change committed so far, revocations included.

## Conformance entry

Called from `finishing-a-development-branch` Step 3.5, before the carried-open menu renders, once per inventory:

1. Draft an item (step 1) for each gap with `recommended: accept`, verdict `DRIFTED` or `PARTIAL`, not `UNAUTHORIZED`, whose `origin` is not an acceptance criterion - the `accept-into-spec` edit built from its `origin` + `evidence`. Every other gap skips the funnel and stays a menu row.
2. Review (step 3), apply and commit (step 5).
3. Re-audit against the amended spec; regenerate the inventory. Only concerns the re-audit closed drop out; sibling concerns keep their rows.
4. Render the disposition menu for what remains - escalated items are ordinary rows there, never a second menu. Rows whose recommended disposition edits the spec carry the readable card fields (`what`, `why`, `Example:`, `Reviewer:`, `Impact:`) on the item, adapted to the numbered item render. A human-selected spec-changing disposition (`accept-into-spec`, `rescope-into-spec`, state-changing `custom`) is already approved: it applies at the protocol's execute-order step 2, bypasses steps 2-4 of this surface, and is recorded as today (`Gn - <title>: <disposition>`); an auto-applied item is recorded `Gn - <title>: accept-into-spec (auto-applied)`.

## Worked example

Eight synthetic items modelled on one real run. Items 1-5 and 8 reach the reviewer; the prefilter catches 6 and 7:

| # | Location | old -> new | Evidence | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Design, parser | parsed with the `AnnouncementList` model -> the `RulesOfProcedureList` model | `rg -n "class .*List" fixtures/rop.html` shows the CMS model name in the page identity block | `auto-apply` |
| 2 | Verification, fixture line | fixture is 41,208 bytes -> 43,117 bytes | `wc -c fixtures/rop-2026-01.html` = 43117 | `auto-apply` |
| 3 | Design, date handling | falls back to the earliest document date -> the latest | fixture rows dated 03-02, 03-05, 03-09; page shows posted 03-09 | `auto-apply` |
| 4 | Design, page identity | assert identity on the `<title>` text -> on the CMS model name | `rg -c "<title>Site</title>" fixtures/` = 4, identical across pages | `auto-apply` |
| 5 | Design, run status | zero new items reports `success` -> `success_empty` | `test_dedup_all_seen` asserts `success_empty` (`tests/test_rop.py:41`) | `auto-apply` |
| 6 | Non-goals | adds "the ROP feed is out of scope for this release" | none | prefiltered: removes approved scope |
| 7 | Acceptance criteria | at least 3 announcements per fetch -> at least 1 | fixture has one item | prefiltered: AC location |
| 8 | Verification, fixture line | 41,208 bytes -> 43,117 bytes | none cited | `escalate` - rubric (a) |

The reviewer clears items 1-5; nothing is applied yet. The batch renders items 6-8 (items 1-5 apply together with the accepted ones after the reply):

```
gauntlet: gate=brainstorming/human-batch
Spec amendments: 3 need your call - from Task 7 BLOCKED; applying as recommended reopens Tasks 4, 6; no phase change.

1. Fewer announcements per fetch - the acceptance criterion drops from at least 3 to at least 1. Lowers the bar you set.
   Only you can change the acceptance criterion.
   Example: 3 items per fetch -> 1
   Reviewer: not reviewed - acceptance-criteria location
   Impact: Acceptance criteria: a fetch yields three or more announcements -> one or more
   A) accept - the spec reads the new text
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: A - the captured fixture has one item; the criterion assumed three
2. Fixture byte count - the verification line changes from 41,208 to 43,117 bytes. The verification line would assert a size nobody measured.
   The reviewer cannot clear a correction without a cited measurement.
   Example: 41,208 bytes -> 43,117 bytes
   Reviewer: rubric (a) fails - no measurement cited for the new byte count
   Impact: Verification: the fixture measures 41,208 bytes -> 43,117 bytes
   A) accept - the spec reads the new text
   B) alt-1 - replace the number with the `wc -c` result
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: B - measure first so the verification line matches the fixture
3. ROP feed out of scope - adds an out-of-scope line for the ROP feed to Non-goals. Drops a deliverable you approved.
   Only you can remove approved scope.
   Example: regulator feed = NERC filings + ROP announcements -> NERC filings only
   Reviewer: not reviewed - removes approved scope
   Impact: Non-goals: the ROP feed ships this release -> (removed)
   A) accept - the spec reads the new text
   Custom: <your own answer> - executed as given; may redirect away from the spec
   Recommended: A - the ROP source has no stable page this release

Reply with one line per item: `1. A`, `2. <your own text>`. Bare `1` takes every recommendation.
Standing grant: reply "auto-apply amends" - every later spec amendment in this flow (corrected facts, paths, verification lines, and scope, acceptance-criteria, or public-contract edits alike) applies without asking; only a redraw (changed problem statement, component added, removed, or re-bounded) still stops for you, and the grant never stands in for a spec approval.

Details
scope: Non-goals - old: (none) -> new: the ROP feed is out of scope for this release
count: Acceptance criteria - old: at least 3 announcements per fetch -> new: at least 1 announcement per fetch
bytes: Verification - old: fixture is 41,208 bytes -> new: fixture is 43,117 bytes
```

Reply `3. keep scope; fix the parser instead` drops item 3 (recorded `scope=custom(keep scope; fix the parser instead)`), returns it to the fix loop, and applies items 1 and 2 as recommended, recorded `count=accept`, `bytes=alt-1`.
